# SECTION 2: SOURCE

## File: src/gitversioned/__init__.py

```python
"""
Versions from git tags for Python, Rust and npm projects in one repository.

gitversioned resolves the version of a checkout from its release tags, stamps it
into every manifest with scoped text edits, validates Conventional Commit titles
and drives a reviewed release: changelog, release pull request and tag.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned import get_version, load_config, resolve

    print(get_version())
    resolved = resolve(load_config())
    print(resolved.version.semver(), resolved.type)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from gitversioned.config import Config, load_config
from gitversioned.errors import (
    CheckFailedError,
    ConfigError,
    EnvironmentProblemError,
    GitVersionedError,
    NothingToReleaseError,
)
from gitversioned.model import Version
from gitversioned.release import ReleasePlan, plan_release
from gitversioned.resolve import Resolved, resolve
from gitversioned.targets import stamp

__all__ = [
    "CheckFailedError",
    "Config",
    "ConfigError",
    "EnvironmentProblemError",
    "GitVersionedError",
    "NothingToReleaseError",
    "ReleasePlan",
    "Resolved",
    "Version",
    "__version__",
    "get_version",
    "load_config",
    "plan_release",
    "resolve",
    "stamp",
]

__version__ = "0.4.0"


def get_version(root: Path | str | None = None, *, standard: str = "pep440") -> str:
    """
    Resolve the version of a project as text.

    :param root: Project folder; defaults to the current one.
    :param standard: ``pep440`` or ``semver``.
    :return: The version of the checkout.
    """
    config = load_config(Path(root) if root is not None else None)
    return resolve(config).version.render(standard)
```

```python
from gitversioned.cli import main

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

## File: src/gitversioned/changelog.py

```python
"""
Changelog sections: entries by kind then scope, rendered and inserted in place.

The layout is fixed. Kinds follow Keep a Changelog; maintenance commits are
hidden unless they are breaking; a ``## Changelog`` block in a pull request body
replaces the entry derived from its title.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.changelog import entries_from_commits, render_section
    from gitversioned.git import Commit
    from gitversioned.model import Version

    entries = entries_from_commits([Commit("abc", "feat(cli): add explain (#41)")])
    print(render_section(Version.parse("1.3.0"), entries, day="2026-11-25"))
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

from gitversioned.commits import NO_RELEASE_TYPES, parse_subject
from gitversioned.git import Commit
from gitversioned.github import PullRequest
from gitversioned.model import Version

__all__ = [
    "KINDS",
    "Entry",
    "entries_from_commits",
    "insert_section",
    "read_section",
    "render_section",
]

KINDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "Added",
    "Changed",
    "Deprecated",
    "Removed",
    "Fixed",
    "Security",
)
_TYPE_KIND: dict[str, str] = {
    "feat": "Added",
    "fix": "Fixed",
    "deprecate": "Deprecated",
    "security": "Security",
    "remove": "Removed",
}
_HEADER = (
    "# Changelog\n\n"
    "All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.\n"
    "The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/) "
    "and the project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).\n\n"
)
_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^## \[?(?P<version>[^\]\s]+)\]?.*$")
_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"(?ims)^#{2,3}\s+changelog\s*$\n(?P<body>.*?)(?=^#{1,2}\s|\Z)")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Entry:
    """
    One line of a changelog section.

    :param kind: Keep a Changelog heading the entry goes under.
    :param scope: Scope shown in bold, when the change has one.
    :param text: What changed.
    :param pr: Pull request number, when known.
    :param breaking: True for a breaking change.
    """

    kind: str
    scope: str | None
    text: str
    pr: int | None = None
    breaking: bool = False


def _from_block(
    body: str, default_kind: str, scope: str | None, pr: int | None
) -> list[Entry]:
    """Read the entries of a ``## Changelog`` block in a pull request body."""
    match = _BLOCK_RE.search(body.replace("\r\n", "\n"))
    if match is None:
        return []
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    kind = default_kind
    for line in match["body"].splitlines():
        heading = re.match(r"^#{3,4}\s+(?P<kind>\w+)\s*$", line.strip())
        if heading:
            name = heading["kind"].capitalize()
            kind = name if name in KINDS else kind
            continue
        bullet = re.match(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(?P<text>.+)$", line)
        if bullet:
            entries.append(Entry(kind, scope, bullet["text"].strip(), pr))
    return entries


def entries_from_commits(
    commits: list[Commit], pull_requests: dict[int, PullRequest] | None = None
) -> list[Entry]:
    """
    Turn commits into changelog entries.

    A pull request title replaces its squash commit subject, and a
    ``## Changelog`` block in the pull request body replaces both.

    :param commits: Commits since the previous release, newest first.
    :param pull_requests: Pull requests by number, when GitHub was reachable.
    :return: Entries in commit order, oldest first, with hidden types left out.
    """
    known = pull_requests or {}
    entries: list[Entry] = []
    for commit in reversed(commits):
        parsed = parse_subject(commit.subject, commit.body, commit.sha)
        number = parsed.pr if parsed else None
        if number is None:
            suffix = re.search(r"\(#(\d+)\)\s*$", commit.subject)
            number = int(suffix.group(1)) if suffix else None
        request = known.get(number) if number is not None else None
        if request is not None:
            retitled = parse_subject(request.title, request.body)
            if retitled is not None:
                parsed = retitled
        if parsed is None:
            continue
        if parsed.type in NO_RELEASE_TYPES and not parsed.breaking:
            continue
        kind = _TYPE_KIND.get(parsed.type, "Changed")
        if request is not None:
            block = _from_block(request.body, kind, parsed.scope, number)
            if block:
                entries.extend(block)
                continue
        entries.append(
            Entry(kind, parsed.scope, parsed.subject, number, parsed.breaking)
        )
    return entries


def render_section(
    version: Version,
    entries: list[Entry],
    *,
    day: str,
    repo_url: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Render one release section.

    :param version: Version being released.
    :param entries: Entries to list.
    :param day: Release date as ``YYYY-MM-DD``.
    :param repo_url: Repository web address, used to link pull requests.
    :return: Markdown ending in a newline.
    """
    lines = [f"## {version.semver()} - {day}", ""]
    for kind in KINDS:
        chosen = [entry for entry in entries if entry.kind == kind]
        if not chosen:
            continue
        chosen.sort(
            key=lambda entry: (
                not entry.breaking,
                entry.scope is None,
                entry.scope or "",
            )
        )
        lines += [f"### {kind}", ""]
        for entry in chosen:
            text = entry.text
            if entry.breaking:
                text = f"**Breaking:** {text}"
            if entry.scope:
                text = f"**{entry.scope}**: {text}"
            if entry.pr is not None:
                link = (
                    f"[#{entry.pr}]({repo_url}/pull/{entry.pr})"
                    if repo_url
                    else f"#{entry.pr}"
                )
                text += f" ({link})"
            lines.append(f"- {text}")
        lines.append("")
    if not entries:
        lines += ["No notable changes.", ""]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _sections(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """List the release sections of a changelog with their spans."""
    matches = list(_SECTION_RE.finditer(text))
    sections: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    for index, match in enumerate(matches):
        end = matches[index + 1].start() if index + 1 < len(matches) else len(text)
        sections.append((match["version"], match.start(), end))
    return sections


def insert_section(text: str, version: Version, section: str) -> str:
    """
    Put a release section into a changelog, touching nothing else.

    A section for the same version is replaced, and pre-release sections of the
    same release are removed, so a release pull request can be rebuilt freely.

    :param text: Current changelog content; empty for a new file.
    :param version: Version of the section.
    :param section: Rendered section.
    :return: The new changelog content.
    """
    if not text.strip():
        text = _HEADER
    for name, start, end in reversed(_sections(text)):
        found = Version.try_parse(name)
        if found is None:
            continue
        if found == version or (
            found.pre is not None and found.release == version.release
        ):
            text = text[:start] + text[end:]
    position = len(text)
    for name, start, _end in _sections(text):
        if Version.try_parse(name) is not None:
            position = start
            break
    before = text[:position]
    if before and not before.endswith("\n\n"):
        before = before.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n"
    after = text[position:]
    block = section.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    return before + block + ("\n" + after if after else "")


def read_section(path: Path, version: Version) -> str | None:
    """
    Read the section of one version back out of a changelog file.

    :param path: Changelog file.
    :param version: Version to find.
    :return: The section text, or ``None``.
    """
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for name, start, end in _sections(text):
        if Version.try_parse(name) == version:
            return text[start:end].strip() + "\n"
    return None
```

## File: src/gitversioned/checks.py

```python
"""
Validation: the repository setup, titles, commit ranges and tag names.

Each function returns findings instead of raising, so the CLI can print every
problem at once and choose the exit code.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.checks import check_title
    from gitversioned.config import load_config

    for finding in check_title(load_config(), "added a thing"):
        print(finding.status, finding.message)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

from gitversioned import git, github
from gitversioned.commits import parse_subject
from gitversioned.config import Config
from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError
from gitversioned.model import Version
from gitversioned.resolve import match_tag, release_tags
from gitversioned.targets import discover

__all__ = [
    "Finding",
    "check_commits",
    "check_repo",
    "check_tag",
    "check_title",
    "worst_exit_code",
]

Status = Literal["ok", "warn", "fail"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Finding:
    """
    One line of a check report.

    :param status: ``ok``, ``warn`` or ``fail``.
    :param area: What was checked.
    :param message: What was found, and the fix when there is one.
    :param exit_code: Exit code this finding asks for when it is a failure.
    """

    status: Status
    area: str
    message: str
    exit_code: int = 1


def worst_exit_code(findings: list[Finding]) -> int:
    """
    :return: The highest exit code among failed findings, or 0.
    """
    return max(
        (item.exit_code for item in findings if item.status == "fail"), default=0
    )


def check_title(config: Config, title: str, area: str = "title") -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate a pull request title or commit subject.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param title: The title to validate.
    :param area: Label for the report line.
    :return: A single ``ok`` finding, or one finding per problem.
    """
    parsed = parse_subject(title)
    if parsed is None:
        return [
            Finding(
                "fail",
                area,
                f"{title!r} is not a Conventional Commit title. Expected "
                f"type(scope): subject. Types: {', '.join(config.types)}.",
            )
        ]
    problems: list[Finding] = []
    if parsed.type not in config.types:
        problems.append(
            Finding(
                "fail",
                area,
                f"unknown type {parsed.type!r}. Types: {', '.join(config.types)}.",
            )
        )
    scopes = config.allowed_scopes()
    if parsed.scope and scopes:
        unknown = [
            scope.strip()
            for scope in parsed.scope.split(",")
            if scope.strip() not in scopes
        ]
        if unknown:
            problems.append(
                Finding(
                    "fail",
                    area,
                    f"unknown scope {unknown[0]!r}. Scopes: {', '.join(scopes)}.",
                )
            )
    return problems or [Finding("ok", area, title)]


def check_commits(config: Config, revision_range: str) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate every commit subject in a git range.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param revision_range: A range such as ``origin/main..HEAD``.
    :return: One finding per invalid commit, or a single ``ok`` finding.
    """
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is None:
        return [Finding("fail", "commits", "not a git repository.", exit_code=3)]
    since, _, ref = revision_range.partition("..")
    if repo.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", since, check=False) is None:
        return [Finding("fail", "commits", f"unknown revision {since!r}.", exit_code=2)]
    commits = repo.commits(since, ref or "HEAD")
    problems: list[Finding] = []
    for commit in commits:
        if commit.subject.startswith(("Merge ", 'Revert "')):
            continue
        found = check_title(config, commit.subject, area=commit.sha[:7])
        problems += [item for item in found if item.status == "fail"]
    return problems or [Finding("ok", "commits", f"{len(commits)} commits")]


def check_tag(
    config: Config, name: str, *, template: str | None = None
) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Validate a tag name and that it is newer than the last release.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param name: Tag name to validate.
    :param template: Tag template to use instead of the configured one.
    :return: A single finding.
    """
    pattern = template or config.tag
    version = match_tag(pattern, name)
    if version is None:
        return [
            Finding(
                "fail",
                "tag",
                f"{name!r} is not a release tag. Expected "
                f"{pattern.replace('{version}', 'X.Y.Z')} with an optional "
                "pre-release such as -rc.1.",
            )
        ]
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    existing: dict[str, Version] = {}
    if repo is not None:
        existing = release_tags(
            pattern, [tag for tag in repo.all_tags() if tag != name]
        )
    if existing:
        latest = max(existing, key=lambda tag: existing[tag].sort_key())
        if version.sort_key() <= existing[latest].sort_key():
            return [
                Finding(
                    "fail",
                    "tag",
                    f"{version.pep440()} is not newer than {latest}.",
                )
            ]
        return [Finding("ok", "tag", f"{version.pep440()}, newer than {latest}")]
    return [Finding("ok", "tag", f"{version.pep440()}, first release")]


def _check_git(config: Config, repo: git.Repo | None) -> Finding:
    """Report whether git history can give a trustworthy version."""
    severity: Status = "fail" if git.is_ci() else "warn"
    if repo is None or repo.head() is None:
        has_other = (
            config.version != "auto"
            or git.read_archive(config.root) is not None
            or git.read_sdist_version(config.root) is not None
        )
        if has_other:
            return Finding(
                "ok",
                "git",
                "no repository; the version comes from a pin, the archive file or "
                "package metadata",
            )
        return Finding(
            severity,
            "git",
            "no git history here and no archive file, so builds use the fallback "
            "version. Set GITVERSIONED__VERSION to pin one.",
            exit_code=3,
        )
    tags = release_tags(config.tag, list(repo.tags_merged()))
    latest = max(tags, key=lambda tag: tags[tag].sort_key()) if tags else None
    if repo.is_shallow() and not tags:
        return Finding(
            severity,
            "git",
            "shallow clone, no tags reachable. Set fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout.",
            exit_code=3,
        )
    if repo.is_shallow():
        return Finding(
            "warn",
            "git",
            f"shallow clone; latest reachable tag {latest}. Commit counts may be "
            "short. Set fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout.",
        )
    if latest:
        return Finding(
            "ok", "git", f"full history, {len(tags)} release tags, latest {latest}"
        )
    return Finding(
        "warn",
        "git",
        f"no release tags match {config.tag!r}; versions start from the fallback "
        f"{config.fallback}.",
    )


def _check_targets(config: Config) -> list[Finding]:
    """Report the files that will be stamped and the allowed scopes."""
    try:
        targets = discover(config)
        for name in config.packages:
            targets += discover(config, package=name)
        scopes = config.allowed_scopes()
    except ConfigError as error:
        return [Finding("fail", "targets", str(error), exit_code=2)]
    root = config.root.resolve()
    names = ", ".join(
        target.path.resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix() for target in targets
    )
    findings = [
        Finding("ok", "targets", names)
        if targets
        else Finding("warn", "targets", "no files to stamp were found.")
    ]
    if scopes:
        findings.append(Finding("ok", "scopes", ", ".join(scopes)))
    return findings


def _check_archive(config: Config, repo: git.Repo) -> Finding:
    """Report whether source tarballs will keep their version."""
    attributes = repo.top / ".gitattributes"
    marked = attributes.is_file() and "export-subst" in attributes.read_text(
        encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"
    )
    if (config.root / git.ARCHIVE_FILE).is_file() and marked:
        return Finding(
            "ok", "archive file", f"{git.ARCHIVE_FILE} and .gitattributes export-subst"
        )
    return Finding(
        "warn",
        "archive file",
        f"{git.ARCHIVE_FILE} is not set up, so source tarballs lose the version. "
        "Run `gitversioned init`.",
    )


def _check_github(config: Config) -> Finding:
    """Report whether the GitHub CLI is usable."""
    if github.available(config.root):
        return Finding("ok", "github", "gh is signed in")
    return Finding(
        "warn",
        "github",
        "gh is missing or not signed in: release --pr and pull request titles in "
        "the changelog are unavailable.",
    )


def check_repo(config: Config) -> list[Finding]:
    """
    Check that the repository can give a trustworthy version.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :return: One finding per area: config, git, targets, archive file, github.
    """
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    findings = [Finding("ok", "config", config.home), _check_git(config, repo)]
    findings += _check_targets(config)
    if repo is not None and repo.head() is not None:
        findings += [_check_archive(config, repo), _check_github(config)]
    return findings
```

## File: src/gitversioned/cli.py

```python
"""
The command line: ``version``, ``check``, ``release`` and the optional ``init``.

Every command accepts ``--root``, ``--package``, ``--json``, ``--verbose`` and
``--quiet``. Exit codes are 0 for success, 1 for a failed check or nothing to
release, 2 for bad usage or configuration and 3 for an environment problem.

Example:
::
    gitversioned version --next --explain
    gitversioned check "feat(cli): add explain"
    gitversioned release --pr
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import functools
import json
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Any, cast

import typer

from gitversioned import __version__, git
from gitversioned.checks import (
    Finding,
    check_commits,
    check_repo,
    check_tag,
    check_title,
    worst_exit_code,
)
from gitversioned.commits import env_bump, next_version
from gitversioned.config import Config, load_config
from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError, GitVersionedError
from gitversioned.logging import configure_logging
from gitversioned.model import Version
from gitversioned.release import (
    open_release_pr,
    package_context,
    plan_release,
    tag_release,
    write_release,
)
from gitversioned.resolve import BuildType, Resolved, resolve
from gitversioned.scaffold import scaffold
from gitversioned.targets import Change, stamp

__all__ = ["app", "main"]

app = typer.Typer(
    name="gitversioned",
    help="Versions from git tags, stamped into every manifest, checked and released.",
    add_completion=False,
    no_args_is_help=True,
    pretty_exceptions_enable=False,
    rich_markup_mode=None,
)

RootOpt = Annotated[
    Path | None,
    typer.Option("--root", "-C", help="Run as if started in DIR.", metavar="DIR"),
]
PackageOpt = Annotated[
    str | None,
    typer.Option(
        "--package", "-p", help="Act on one package from [packages].", metavar="NAME"
    ),
]
JsonOpt = Annotated[
    bool, typer.Option("--json", help="Machine-readable output on stdout.")
]
VerboseOpt = Annotated[
    int,
    typer.Option(
        "--verbose", "-v", count=True, help="More detail on stderr (-vv for debug)."
    ),
]
QuietOpt = Annotated[bool, typer.Option("--quiet", "-q", help="Errors only.")]

_LEVELS = ("major", "minor", "patch")
_PRE = ("rc", "beta", "alpha")
_TYPES = ("dev", "nightly", "release")
_STANDARDS = ("pep440", "semver")
_MAX_LISTED = 5


def _print_version(value: bool) -> None:
    """Print the version of gitversioned itself and stop."""
    if value:
        typer.echo(f"gitversioned v{__version__}")
        raise typer.Exit


@app.callback()
def _root(
    version: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option(
            "--version",
            help="Print the version of gitversioned itself.",
            callback=_print_version,
            is_eager=True,
        ),
    ] = False,
) -> None:
    """Versions from git tags, stamped into every manifest, checked and released."""


def _choice(value: str | None, allowed: tuple[str, ...], flag: str) -> str | None:
    """Validate an option that takes one of a few words."""
    if value is not None and value not in allowed:
        raise ConfigError(f"{flag} must be one of: {', '.join(allowed)}.")
    return value


def _emit(data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Print a JSON document."""
    typer.echo(json.dumps(data, indent=2))


def _fail(error: GitVersionedError, as_json: bool) -> None:
    """Report an error and exit with its code."""
    if as_json:
        _emit({"ok": False, "error": str(error), "exit_code": error.exit_code})
    else:
        typer.echo(f"fail  {error}", err=True)
    raise typer.Exit(error.exit_code)


def _command(function: Callable[..., None]) -> Callable[..., None]:
    """Give a command logging setup and uniform error handling."""

    @functools.wraps(function)
    def wrapper(*args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        verbosity = -1 if kwargs.get("quiet") else int(kwargs.get("verbose") or 0)
        configure_logging(verbosity)
        try:
            function(*args, **kwargs)
        except GitVersionedError as error:
            _fail(error, bool(kwargs.get("json_output")))

    return wrapper


def _default_standard(config: Config) -> str:
    """Pick PEP 440 for a Python project and SemVer otherwise."""
    pyproject = config.root / "pyproject.toml"
    if pyproject.is_file() and "[project]" in pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
        return "pep440"
    return "semver"


def _branch_name(config: Config) -> str:
    """Name the branch the release branch was rebuilt from."""
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    return (repo.branch() if repo is not None else None) or "HEAD"


def _next(
    config: Config, resolved: Resolved, bump: str | None, pre: str | None
) -> Version:
    """Compute the next release version for the ``version --next`` path."""
    override = bump or env_bump()
    explicit = override if override and override not in _LEVELS else None
    return next_version(
        resolved.base,
        resolved.known,
        resolved.plan,
        fallback=Version.parse(config.fallback),
        explicit=explicit,
        bump=override if explicit is None else None,
        pre=pre,
    )


def _explain(
    config: Config, resolved: Resolved, upcoming: Version | None, standard: str
) -> list[str]:
    """Build the lines of an ``--explain`` report."""
    lines: list[str] = []
    if upcoming is not None:
        lines.append(f"next      {upcoming.render(standard)}")
    else:
        shown = resolved.version.render(standard)
        lines.append(f"version   {shown}")
        lines.append(f"type      {resolved.type}")
    if resolved.base is not None:
        where = f"tag {resolved.tag}" if resolved.tag else resolved.source
        sha = f", {resolved.short_sha}" if resolved.short_sha else ""
        lines.append(
            f"current   {resolved.base.render(standard)}  "
            f"({where}{sha}, "
            f"{resolved.distance} commits since)"
        )
    else:
        lines.append(f"current   none ({resolved.source}; fallback {config.fallback})")
    if resolved.plan.reasons:
        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
        for level, _commit in resolved.plan.reasons:
            counts[level or "none"] = counts.get(level or "none", 0) + 1
        summary = ", ".join(f"{count} {name}" for name, count in counts.items())
        lines.append(f"why       {resolved.plan.level or 'no release'}: {summary}")
        for level, commit in resolved.plan.reasons[:20]:
            lines.append(f"  {(level or 'none'):<7} {commit.subject}")
    if resolved.dirty:
        shown = ", ".join(resolved.dirty[:_MAX_LISTED])
        extra = len(resolved.dirty) - _MAX_LISTED
        more = f" and {extra} more" if extra > 0 else ""
        lines.append(f"dirty     {shown}{more}")
    for note in resolved.notes:
        lines.append(f"note      {note}")
    total = len(Config.key_names())
    used = len(config.keys_set)
    lines.append(f"config    {config.home}  ({used} keys set, {total - used} defaults)")
    return lines


@app.command("version")
@_command
def version_command(
    version: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Argument(
            help="Use this version instead of resolving one.", metavar="[VERSION]"
        ),
    ] = None,
    next_release: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--next", help="The version the next release would get.")
    ] = False,
    bump: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--bump", help="With --next: force major, minor or patch.", metavar="LEVEL"
        ),
    ] = None,
    pre: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option("--pre", help="With --next: rc, beta or alpha.", metavar="KIND"),
    ] = None,
    build_type: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option("--type", help="Force dev, nightly or release.", metavar="TYPE"),
    ] = None,
    standard: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option("--standard", help="Print as pep440 or semver.", metavar="STD"),
    ] = None,
    write: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--write", help="Stamp the version into every target.")
    ] = False,
    dry_run: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option("--dry-run", help="With --write: show the diff, change nothing."),
    ] = False,
    explain: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--explain", help="Show how the answer was reached.")
    ] = False,
    root: RootOpt = None,
    package: PackageOpt = None,
    json_output: JsonOpt = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = 0,
    quiet: QuietOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Print the version; --next for the upcoming release; --write to stamp files."""
    _choice(bump, _LEVELS, "--bump")
    _choice(pre, _PRE, "--pre")
    _choice(build_type, _TYPES, "--type")
    _choice(standard, _STANDARDS, "--standard")
    if (bump or pre) and not next_release:
        raise ConfigError("--bump and --pre need --next.")
    if dry_run and not write:
        raise ConfigError("--dry-run needs --write.")
    config = load_config(root)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(
        config,
        pin=version,
        build_type=cast("BuildType | None", build_type),
        tag_template=template,
        path_scope=scope,
    )
    spelling = standard or _default_standard(config)
    upcoming: Version | None = None
    if next_release:
        upcoming = _next(config, resolved, bump, pre)
        resolved = dataclasses.replace(resolved, version=upcoming, type="release")
    changes = stamp(config, resolved, dry_run=dry_run, package=package) if write else []
    if json_output:
        _emit(_version_json(resolved, spelling, changes))
        return
    if explain:
        for line in _explain(config, resolved, upcoming, spelling):
            typer.echo(line)
    else:
        typer.echo(resolved.version.render(spelling))
    if write:
        _print_changes(changes, dry_run)


def _version_json(
    resolved: Resolved, spelling: str, changes: list[Change]
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Build the JSON document for the version command."""
    shown = resolved.version
    return {
        "version": shown.render(spelling),
        "pep440": shown.pep440(),
        "semver": shown.semver(),
        "type": resolved.type,
        "source": resolved.source,
        "tag": resolved.tag,
        "distance": resolved.distance,
        "sha": resolved.short_sha,
        "dirty": bool(resolved.dirty),
        "warnings": resolved.warnings,
        "written": [
            {
                "path": change.path,
                "old": change.old,
                "new": change.new,
                "changed": bool(change.diff),
            }
            for change in changes
        ],
    }


def _print_changes(changes: list[Change], dry_run: bool) -> None:
    """Print what stamping did, or the diffs for a dry run."""
    if dry_run:
        for change in changes:
            if change.diff:
                typer.echo(change.diff, nl=False)
        return
    width = max((len(change.path) for change in changes), default=0)
    for change in changes:
        state = change.new if change.diff else f"{change.new} (unchanged)"
        typer.echo(f"  {change.path:<{width}}  {state}")
    if not changes:
        typer.echo("  no targets found", err=True)


def _report(findings: list[Finding], as_json: bool, warn_only: bool) -> None:
    """Print findings and exit with the right code."""
    code = worst_exit_code(findings)
    if as_json:
        _emit(
            {
                "ok": code == 0,
                "findings": [
                    {"status": item.status, "area": item.area, "message": item.message}
                    for item in findings
                ],
            }
        )
    else:
        simple = (
            len(findings) == 1
            and findings[0].status == "ok"
            and findings[0].area == "title"
        )
        if simple:
            typer.echo("ok")
        else:
            width = max(len(item.area) for item in findings)
            for item in findings:
                typer.echo(
                    f"{item.status:<5} {item.area:<{width}}  {item.message}",
                    err=item.status == "fail",
                )
    if code and not warn_only:
        raise typer.Exit(code)


@app.command("check")
@_command
def check_command(
    title: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Argument(
            help="A pull request title or commit subject to validate.",
            metavar="[TITLE]",
        ),
    ] = None,
    commits: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--commits",
            help="Validate every commit subject in a git range.",
            metavar="RANGE",
        ),
    ] = None,
    tag: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option("--tag", help="Validate a tag name.", metavar="NAME"),
    ] = None,
    file: Annotated[
        Path | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--file",
            help="Read the message from a file (commit-msg hook).",
            metavar="PATH",
        ),
    ] = None,
    warn: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--warn", help="Report problems but exit 0.")
    ] = False,
    root: RootOpt = None,
    package: PackageOpt = None,
    json_output: JsonOpt = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = 0,
    quiet: QuietOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Validate the repo setup, a pull request title, commits or a tag."""
    if sum(item is not None for item in (title, commits, tag, file)) > 1:
        raise ConfigError("give one of TITLE, --commits, --tag or --file.")
    config = load_config(root)
    if file is not None:
        try:
            lines = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        except OSError as error:
            raise ConfigError(f"cannot read {file}: {error}") from error
        title = next(
            (line for line in lines if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")), ""
        )
    if title is not None:
        findings = check_title(config, title)
    elif commits is not None:
        findings = check_commits(config, commits)
    elif tag is not None:
        template, _scope = package_context(config, package)
        findings = check_tag(config, tag, template=template)
    else:
        findings = check_repo(config)
    _report(findings, json_output, warn)


@app.command("release")
@_command
def release_command(
    version: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Argument(help="Release exactly this version.", metavar="[VERSION]"),
    ] = None,
    bump: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--bump",
            help="Override the level chosen from commits and labels.",
            metavar="LEVEL",
        ),
    ] = None,
    pre: Annotated[
        str | None,
        typer.Option(
            "--pre", help="Make it a pre-release: rc, beta or alpha.", metavar="KIND"
        ),
    ] = None,
    write: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option(
            "--write",
            help="Update the changelog and committed targets in the working tree.",
        ),
    ] = False,
    pr: Annotated[
        bool,
        typer.Option(
            "--pr",
            help="Commit the release to the release branch and open or update the PR.",
        ),
    ] = False,
    tag: Annotated[
        bool, typer.Option("--tag", help="Tag the release commit and push the tag.")
    ] = False,
    root: RootOpt = None,
    package: PackageOpt = None,
    json_output: JsonOpt = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = 0,
    quiet: QuietOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Plan a release; --pr to open the release pull request; --tag to tag it."""
    _choice(bump, _LEVELS, "--bump")
    _choice(pre, _PRE, "--pre")
    if sum((write, pr, tag)) > 1:
        raise ConfigError("give one of --write, --pr or --tag.")
    config = load_config(root)
    if tag:
        if bump or pre:
            raise ConfigError("--tag takes a VERSION, not --bump or --pre.")
        name, sha, pushed = tag_release(config, version=version, package=package)
        if json_output:
            _emit({"stage": "tag", "tag": name, "sha": sha, "pushed": pushed})
        else:
            typer.echo(
                f"tag       {name} at {sha[:7]}, "
                f"{'pushed' if pushed else 'created locally'}"
            )
        return
    if pr:
        plan, request, opened = open_release_pr(
            config,
            version=version,
            bump=bump,
            pre=pre,
            package=package,
        )
        if json_output:
            _emit(
                {
                    "stage": "pr",
                    "version": plan.version.pep440(),
                    "tag": plan.tag,
                    "branch": plan.branch,
                    "title": plan.title,
                    "files": plan.files,
                    "pr": {
                        "number": request.number,
                        "url": request.url,
                        "opened": opened,
                    },
                }
            )
        else:
            typer.echo(f"release   {plan.version.pep440()}")
            typer.echo(
                f"branch    {plan.branch}  (rebuilt from {_branch_name(config)})"
            )
            typer.echo(f"commit    {plan.title}")
            typer.echo(
                f"pr        #{request.number} "
                f"{'opened' if opened else 'updated'}  {request.url}"
            )
        return
    plan = plan_release(
        config,
        version=version,
        bump=bump,
        pre=pre,
        package=package,
    )
    changed = write_release(config, plan) if write else []
    if json_output:
        _emit(
            {
                "stage": "write" if write else "plan",
                "version": plan.version.pep440(),
                "semver": plan.version.semver(),
                "previous": plan.previous.pep440() if plan.previous else None,
                "tag": plan.tag,
                "level": plan.level,
                "files": plan.files,
                "changed": changed,
                "changelog": plan.section,
            }
        )
        return
    typer.echo(f"release   {plan.version.pep440()}  ({plan.level})")
    typer.echo(f"tag       {plan.tag}")
    typer.echo(f"files     {', '.join(plan.files) or 'none'}")
    typer.echo("")
    typer.echo(plan.section)
    if write:
        typer.echo(f"Wrote {', '.join(changed) or 'nothing (already up to date)'}.")
    else:
        typer.echo("Nothing changed. Run with --write, --pr or --tag.")


@app.command("init")
@_command
def init_command(
    root: RootOpt = None,
    json_output: JsonOpt = False,
    verbose: VerboseOpt = 0,
    quiet: QuietOpt = False,
) -> None:
    """Optional: add the archive file and wire up the build backend."""
    config = load_config(root)
    actions = scaffold(config)
    if json_output:
        _emit(
            {
                "actions": [
                    {"action": action, "path": path, "detail": detail}
                    for action, path, detail in actions
                ]
            }
        )
        return
    for action, path, detail in actions:
        typer.echo(f"{action:<5}  {path:<22}{('  ' + detail) if detail else ''}")
    if not config.keys_set:
        typer.echo(
            "No gitversioned settings needed: defaults and discovery cover this repo."
        )


def main() -> None:
    """Run the command line."""
    app()
```

## File: src/gitversioned/commits.py

```python
"""
Conventional Commit parsing and the rules that choose the next version.

The rules are fixed: a breaking change raises major, ``feat`` raises minor, any
other change raises patch, and ``chore``, ``ci``, ``test`` and ``release`` commits
alone do not justify a release. Below 1.0 every level shifts down by one.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.commits import parse_subject, level_of

    parsed = parse_subject("feat(cli)!: drop the old commands (#12)")
    assert parsed is not None and parsed.breaking and parsed.pr == 12
    assert level_of(parsed) == "major"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass

from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError, NothingToReleaseError
from gitversioned.git import Commit
from gitversioned.model import Level, Version

__all__ = [
    "NO_RELEASE_TYPES",
    "BumpPlan",
    "ParsedCommit",
    "env_bump",
    "level_of",
    "next_version",
    "parse_subject",
    "plan_bump",
]

NO_RELEASE_TYPES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"chore", "ci", "test", "release"})
_LEVEL_RANK: dict[str, int] = {"patch": 1, "minor": 2, "major": 3}

_SUBJECT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<type>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]*)"
    r"(?:\((?P<scope>[^()\r\n]+)\))?"
    r"(?P<breaking>!)?: (?P<subject>\S.*)$"
)
_PR_RE = re.compile(r"\s*\(#(?P<pr>\d+)\)\s*$")
_BREAKING_RE = re.compile(r"^BREAKING[ -]CHANGE: ", re.MULTILINE)
_MERGE_RE = re.compile(r"^Merge (branch|pull request|remote-tracking branch|tag) ")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ParsedCommit:
    """
    A commit subject split into its Conventional Commit parts.

    :param type: Commit type in lower case, such as ``feat``.
    :param scope: Scope in parentheses, when present.
    :param breaking: True for a ``!`` marker or a ``BREAKING CHANGE:`` footer.
    :param subject: Description after the colon, without the pull request suffix.
    :param pr: Pull request number from a ``(#N)`` suffix, when present.
    :param sha: Commit hash, when the subject came from a commit.
    """

    type: str
    scope: str | None
    breaking: bool
    subject: str
    pr: int | None = None
    sha: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BumpPlan:
    """
    The level a set of commits asks for and the reason per commit.

    :param level: The highest level found, or ``None`` when nothing is releasable.
    :param reasons: Each commit with the level it contributes.
    """

    level: Level | None
    reasons: tuple[tuple[Level | None, Commit], ...]


def parse_subject(
    subject: str, body: str = "", sha: str | None = None
) -> ParsedCommit | None:
    """
    Parse a commit subject or pull request title.

    :param subject: First line of the message.
    :param body: Rest of the message, searched for a breaking-change footer.
    :param sha: Commit hash to carry along.
    :return: The parsed parts, or ``None`` when the subject is not conventional.
    """
    match = _SUBJECT_RE.match(subject.strip())
    if match is None:
        return None
    text = match["subject"]
    pr: int | None = None
    pr_match = _PR_RE.search(text)
    if pr_match:
        pr = int(pr_match["pr"])
        text = text[: pr_match.start()]
    return ParsedCommit(
        type=match["type"].lower(),
        scope=match["scope"].strip() if match["scope"] else None,
        breaking=bool(match["breaking"]) or bool(_BREAKING_RE.search(body)),
        subject=text.strip(),
        pr=pr,
        sha=sha,
    )


def level_of(parsed: ParsedCommit | None, subject: str = "") -> Level | None:
    """
    Decide the level one commit asks for.

    :param parsed: The parsed commit, or ``None`` for an unconventional subject.
    :param subject: The raw subject, used to skip merge commits.
    :return: ``major``, ``minor``, ``patch`` or ``None`` for no release.
    """
    if parsed is None:
        return None if _MERGE_RE.match(subject) else "patch"
    if parsed.breaking:
        return "major"
    if parsed.type == "feat":
        return "minor"
    if parsed.type in NO_RELEASE_TYPES:
        return None
    return "patch"


def plan_bump(commits: list[Commit]) -> BumpPlan:
    """
    Find the highest level a list of commits asks for.

    :param commits: Commits since the last release.
    :return: The level and the per-commit reasons.
    """
    reasons: list[tuple[Level | None, Commit]] = []
    best: Level | None = None
    for commit in commits:
        level = level_of(parse_subject(commit.subject, commit.body), commit.subject)
        reasons.append((level, commit))
        if level is not None and (
            best is None or _LEVEL_RANK[level] > _LEVEL_RANK[best]
        ):
            best = level
    return BumpPlan(level=best, reasons=tuple(reasons))


def _shift(level: str, current: Version) -> str:
    """Shift a commit-derived level down by one for a version below 1.0."""
    if current.major > 0:
        return level
    return {"major": "minor", "minor": "patch", "patch": "patch"}[level]


def env_bump() -> str | None:
    """
    :return: The ``GITVERSIONED__BUMP`` override, a level or a version, if set.
    """
    return os.environ.get("GITVERSIONED__BUMP", "").strip() or None


def next_version(
    current: Version | None,
    known: list[Version],
    plan: BumpPlan,
    *,
    fallback: Version,
    explicit: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
) -> Version:
    """
    Choose the next release version.

    Overrides win in this order: an explicit version, an explicit level, then the
    commits. A pre-release numbers itself after the existing tags of its kind.

    :param current: The latest released version, or ``None`` before the first tag.
    :param known: Every version already tagged, used to number pre-releases.
    :param plan: What the commits ask for.
    :param fallback: First version of a repository with no tags.
    :param explicit: A version to release exactly, or a level name.
    :param bump: A level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the result a pre-release of this kind.
    :return: The version to release.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If no override is given and no commit is
        releasable.
    :raises ConfigError: If an override is neither a level nor a version.
    """
    if explicit and explicit not in _LEVEL_RANK:
        target = Version.parse(explicit)
        if pre is None:
            return target
        target = target.release
    else:
        level_name = explicit or bump
        if level_name is not None and level_name not in _LEVEL_RANK:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"not a bump level: {level_name!r}. Use major, minor or patch."
            )
        if current is None:
            target = fallback.release
        elif current.pre is not None and level_name is None:
            target = current.release
        elif level_name is not None:
            target = current.release.bump(level_name)
        elif plan.level is None:
            raise NothingToReleaseError("Nothing to release: no releasable commits.")
        else:
            target = current.bump(_shift(plan.level, current))
    if pre is None:
        return target
    numbers = [
        version.pre[1]
        for version in known
        if version.pre is not None
        and version.dev is None
        and version.pre[0] == pre
        and version.release == target
    ]
    return target.with_parts(pre=(pre, max(numbers, default=0) + 1))
```

## File: src/gitversioned/config.py

```python
"""
The configuration model, its homes and its environment overrides.

A repository keeps its settings in exactly one home. The model has twelve root
keys, four keys per target and two per package; unknown keys are errors, and any
root key can be overridden with ``GITVERSIONED__KEY`` in the environment.

Example:
::
    from pathlib import Path
    from gitversioned.config import load_config

    config = load_config(Path.cwd())
    print(config.home, config.tag, config.scopes)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import configparser
import difflib
import json
import os
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Annotated, Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, ValidationError, model_validator

from gitversioned import git
from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError

if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    import tomllib
else:  # pragma: no cover
    import tomli as tomllib

__all__ = [
    "DEFAULT_TYPES",
    "ENV_PREFIX",
    "Config",
    "PackageConfig",
    "TargetConfig",
    "find_homes",
    "find_root",
    "load_config",
]

ENV_PREFIX: Annotated[str, "Prefix of every environment override"] = "GITVERSIONED__"
DEFAULT_TYPES: Annotated[tuple[str, ...], "Commit types the template allows"] = (
    "feat",
    "fix",
    "perf",
    "refactor",
    "docs",
    "test",
    "build",
    "ci",
    "chore",
    "revert",
    "deprecate",
    "release",
)

BumpBase = Literal["patch", "minor", "major", "next"]


class TargetConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    A file to stamp that discovery cannot find on its own.

    :param path: File to stamp, relative to the project root.
    :param key: Dotted path of the value in a TOML, JSON or YAML file.
    :param pattern: Regular expression with a ``version`` group, for any text file.
    :param commit: Whether the release pull request commits the file; the default
        depends on the kind of file.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    path: str
    key: str | None = None
    pattern: str | None = None
    commit: bool | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _one_locator(self) -> TargetConfig:
        if self.key and self.pattern:
            raise ValueError("a target takes `key` or `pattern`, not both")
        return self


class PackageConfig(BaseModel):
    """
    A package with its own folder and, optionally, its own tag.

    :param path: Package folder, relative to the project root.
    :param tag: Tag template such as ``core-v{version}``; without it the package
        follows the repository version.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    path: str
    tag: str | None = None

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _tag_template(self) -> PackageConfig:
        if self.tag is not None and "{version}" not in self.tag:
            raise ValueError("`tag` must contain {version}")
        return self


class Config(BaseModel):
    """
    Every setting gitversioned has.

    :param version: A pinned version, or ``auto`` to resolve from git.
    :param fallback: Base version when no tag exists yet.
    :param tag: Tag template; also how release tags are recognised.
    :param annotated: Create annotated tags carrying the changelog section.
    :param branch: Branch releases are cut from.
    :param dev: Base of a development build.
    :param nightly: Base of a nightly build.
    :param date: Date used in development and nightly versions.
    :param local: Add the commit hash to development builds.
    :param changelog: Changelog file, or ``False`` to turn it off.
    :param types: Allowed commit types.
    :param scopes: Allowed scopes, or a TOML file whose table names are the scopes.
    :param targets: Extra files to stamp.
    :param packages: Packages with their own folder and optional tag.
    :param root: Project root the paths are relative to.
    :param home: Where the settings were read from, for messages.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    version: str = "auto"
    fallback: str = "0.1.0"
    tag: str = "v{version}"
    annotated: bool = False
    branch: str = "main"
    dev: BumpBase = "patch"
    nightly: BumpBase = "next"
    date: Literal["commit", "build"] = "commit"
    local: bool = True
    changelog: str | Literal[False] = "CHANGELOG.md"
    types: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: list(DEFAULT_TYPES))
    scopes: list[str] | str = Field(default_factory=list)
    targets: list[TargetConfig] = Field(default_factory=list)
    packages: dict[str, PackageConfig] = Field(default_factory=dict)

    root: Path = Field(default_factory=Path.cwd, exclude=True)
    home: str = Field(default="defaults", exclude=True)
    keys_set: tuple[str, ...] = Field(default=(), exclude=True)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _tag_template(self) -> Config:
        if "{version}" not in self.tag:
            raise ValueError("`tag` must contain {version}")
        return self

    def allowed_scopes(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        Resolve the allowed scopes, reading the scopes file when one is named.

        Package names are always allowed once any scope is restricted.

        :return: Scope names; an empty list allows any scope.
        :raises ConfigError: If the scopes file is missing or not valid TOML.
        """
        if isinstance(self.scopes, list):
            scopes = list(self.scopes)
        else:
            path = self.root / self.scopes
            try:
                data = tomllib.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError) as error:
                raise ConfigError(f"cannot read scopes file {path}: {error}") from error
            scopes = [key for key, value in data.items() if isinstance(value, dict)]
        if scopes:
            scopes += [name for name in self.packages if name not in scopes]
        return scopes

    @classmethod
    def key_names(cls) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: The names of the settings a home may hold.
        """
        return [name for name, field in cls.model_fields.items() if not field.exclude]


_HOME_ORDER = (
    ".config/gitversioned.toml",
    "gitversioned.toml",
    "pyproject.toml",
    "Cargo.toml",
    "package.json",
    "setup.cfg",
)


def _pyproject_table(path: Path, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Read ``[tool.gitversioned]`` from a pyproject file."""
    table = tomllib.loads(text).get("tool", {}).get("gitversioned")
    return (f"{path} [tool.gitversioned]", table) if table is not None else None


def _cargo_table(path: Path, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Read the gitversioned metadata table from a Cargo manifest."""
    data = tomllib.loads(text)
    for section in ("workspace", "package"):
        table = data.get(section, {}).get("metadata", {}).get("gitversioned")
        if table is not None:
            return f"{path} [{section}.metadata.gitversioned]", table
    return None


def _npm_table(path: Path, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Read the ``gitversioned`` key from a package.json file."""
    table = json.loads(text).get("gitversioned")
    return (f'{path} "gitversioned"', table) if table is not None else None


def _setup_cfg_table(path: Path, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Read ``[tool:gitversioned]`` from a setup.cfg file."""
    parser = configparser.ConfigParser()
    parser.read_string(text)
    if not parser.has_section("tool:gitversioned"):
        return None
    table = {key: _coerce(value) for key, value in parser["tool:gitversioned"].items()}
    return f"{path} [tool:gitversioned]", table


def _own_file_table(path: Path, text: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Read a gitversioned.toml file, which is settings from top to bottom."""
    return str(path), tomllib.loads(text)


_HOME_READERS: dict[str, Callable[[Path, str], tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None]] = {
    "gitversioned.toml": _own_file_table,
    "pyproject.toml": _pyproject_table,
    "Cargo.toml": _cargo_table,
    "package.json": _npm_table,
    "setup.cfg": _setup_cfg_table,
}


def _read_home(path: Path) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]] | None:
    """Return the label and settings table of a home file, if it holds one."""
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except OSError:
        return None
    try:
        return _HOME_READERS[path.name](path, text)
    except (tomllib.TOMLDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError, configparser.Error) as error:
        raise ConfigError(f"cannot parse {path}: {error}") from error


def _coerce(value: str) -> Any:
    """Turn an environment or INI string into a typed value when it is JSON."""
    text = value.strip()
    try:
        return json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return text


def find_homes(root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
    """
    Find every config home in a folder that holds settings.

    :param root: Folder to look in.
    :return: A label and settings table per home, in priority order.
    """
    homes: list[tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]] = []
    for relative in _HOME_ORDER:
        found = _read_home(root / relative)
        if found is not None:
            homes.append(found)
    return homes


def find_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    """
    Find the project root for a starting folder.

    The root is the nearest parent holding a config home, searching no higher
    than the repository root; failing that the repository root, then the start.

    :param start: Folder the command was started in.
    :return: The project root.
    """
    start = start.resolve()
    repo = git.Repo.open(start)
    top = repo.top if repo is not None else None
    current = start
    while True:
        if find_homes(current):
            return current
        if current in (top, current.parent):
            break
        current = current.parent
    return top if top is not None and _inside(start, top) else start


def _inside(path: Path, parent: Path) -> bool:
    """Return whether a path is the parent or below it."""
    try:
        path.relative_to(parent)
    except ValueError:
        return False
    return True


def _suggest(name: str, valid: list[str]) -> str:
    """Return a hint naming the nearest valid key."""
    close = difflib.get_close_matches(name, valid, n=1)
    return f" Did you mean `{close[0]}`?" if close else ""


def load_config(
    start: Path | None = None, *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None
) -> Config:
    """
    Load the configuration for a project.

    :param start: Folder the command was started in; defaults to the current one.
    :param env: Environment to read overrides from; defaults to ``os.environ``.
    :return: The validated configuration.
    :raises ConfigError: For two homes, an unknown key or an invalid value.
    """
    environment = os.environ if env is None else env
    root = find_root(start or Path.cwd())
    homes = find_homes(root)
    if len(homes) > 1:
        names = " and ".join(label for label, _ in homes)
        raise ConfigError(
            f"settings found in two homes: {names}. Keep them in one file."
        )
    label, table = homes[0] if homes else ("defaults", {})
    if not isinstance(table, dict):
        raise ConfigError(f"{label} must be a table")
    data: dict[str, Any] = dict(table)
    valid = Config.key_names()
    for name in data:
        if name not in valid:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"unknown key `{name}` in {label}.{_suggest(name, valid)} "
                f"Valid keys: {', '.join(valid)}."
            )
    keys_set = sorted(data)
    for name, value in environment.items():
        if not name.startswith(ENV_PREFIX):
            continue
        key = name[len(ENV_PREFIX) :].lower()
        if key == "bump":
            continue
        if key not in valid:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"unknown environment override {name}.{_suggest(key, valid)}"
            )
        data[key] = _coerce(value) if key not in ("version", "fallback") else value
        keys_set.append(f"{key} (env)")
    try:
        config = Config(**data)
    except ValidationError as error:
        problems = "; ".join(
            f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item['loc']) or 'config'}: {item['msg']}"
            for item in error.errors()
        )
        raise ConfigError(f"invalid config in {label}: {problems}") from error
    config.root = root
    config.home = label
    config.keys_set = tuple(keys_set)
    return config
```

## File: src/gitversioned/editors.py

```python
"""
Locators that find a single value inside a text file without parsing and
re-serialising the file.

Each function returns the character span of a value, so a caller can replace
that span and leave every other byte of the file untouched: comments, key order,
quoting and line endings all survive.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.editors import toml_span

    text = '[package]\\nname = "demo"\\nversion = "1.0.0"  # keep\\n'
    start, end = toml_span(text, ["package", "version"])
    assert text[start:end] == "1.0.0"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

__all__ = ["json_span", "toml_span", "toml_table_spans", "yaml_span"]

_TOML_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\s*\[\[?\s*(?P<name>[^\]]+?)\s*\]\]?\s*(?:#.*)?$")


def _toml_key_pattern(key: str) -> re.Pattern[str]:
    """Build the pattern matching ``key = "value"`` with bare or quoted key parts."""
    parts = [rf"""["']?{re.escape(part)}["']?""" for part in key.split(".")]
    return re.compile(
        r"^(?P<lead>\s*"
        + r"\s*\.\s*".join(parts)
        + r"""\s*=\s*)(?P<q>["'])(?P<value>.*?)(?P=q)"""
    )


def _normal_table(name: str) -> str:
    """Normalise a TOML table name by dropping quotes and spaces around dots."""
    return ".".join(part.strip().strip("\"'") for part in name.split("."))


def toml_table_spans(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int, int]]:
    """
    List the tables of a TOML document with the span of each body.

    :param text: TOML source.
    :return: Table name, body start and body end; the root table is named ``""``.
    """
    tables: list[tuple[str, int, int]] = []
    name = ""
    start = 0
    offset = 0
    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        match = _TOML_HEADER.match(line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if match and "=" not in line.split("#")[0].split("]")[-1]:
            tables.append((name, start, offset))
            name = _normal_table(match["name"])
            start = offset + len(line)
        offset += len(line)
    tables.append((name, start, len(text)))
    return tables


def toml_span(text: str, path: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """
    Find a string value in a TOML document by dotted path.

    The path is split into a table and a key at every possible point, so
    ``["tool", "poetry", "version"]`` finds ``version`` under ``[tool.poetry]``
    and also ``poetry.version`` under ``[tool]``.

    :param text: TOML source.
    :param path: Keys from the root to the value.
    :return: Start and end of the value between its quotes, or ``None``.
    """
    tables = toml_table_spans(text)
    for split in range(len(path) - 1, -1, -1):
        table = ".".join(path[:split])
        pattern = _toml_key_pattern(".".join(path[split:]))
        for name, start, end in tables:
            if name != table:
                continue
            offset = start
            for line in text[start:end].splitlines(keepends=True):
                match = pattern.match(line)
                if match:
                    return offset + match.start("value"), offset + match.end("value")
                offset += len(line)
    return None


class _JsonScanner:
    """A minimal JSON walker that records where string values sit."""

    def __init__(self, text: str) -> None:
        self.text = text
        self.pos = 0
        self.spans: dict[tuple[str, ...], tuple[int, int]] = {}

    def _space(self) -> None:
        while self.pos < len(self.text) and self.text[self.pos] in " \t\r\n":
            self.pos += 1

    def _string(self) -> tuple[int, int]:
        self.pos += 1
        start = self.pos
        while self.text[self.pos] != '"':
            self.pos += 2 if self.text[self.pos] == "\\" else 1
        end = self.pos
        self.pos += 1
        return start, end

    def value(self, path: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
        """Walk one value, recording string spans under their path."""
        self._space()
        char = self.text[self.pos]
        if char == '"':
            self.spans[path] = self._string()
        elif char == "{":
            self.pos += 1
            self._space()
            while self.text[self.pos] != "}":
                self._space()
                start, end = self._string()
                key = self.text[start:end]
                self._space()
                self.pos += 1
                self.value((*path, key))
                self._space()
                if self.text[self.pos] == ",":
                    self.pos += 1
                    self._space()
            self.pos += 1
        elif char == "[":
            self.pos += 1
            index = 0
            self._space()
            while self.text[self.pos] != "]":
                self.value((*path, str(index)))
                index += 1
                self._space()
                if self.text[self.pos] == ",":
                    self.pos += 1
                    self._space()
            self.pos += 1
        else:
            while self.pos < len(self.text) and self.text[self.pos] not in ",}] \t\r\n":
                self.pos += 1


def json_span(text: str, path: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """
    Find a string value in a JSON document by key path.

    :param text: JSON source.
    :param path: Keys, and list indexes as digits, from the root to the value.
    :return: Start and end of the value between its quotes, or ``None`` when the
        path is absent, not a string, or the document is malformed.
    """
    scanner = _JsonScanner(text)
    try:
        scanner.value(())
    except IndexError:
        return None
    return scanner.spans.get(tuple(path))


_YAML_LINE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<indent>\s*)(?P<key>[^\s#:][^:#]*?)\s*:(?:\s+(?P<rest>.*))?$"
)


def _yaml_scalar(rest: str, base: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """Return the span of a scalar within the text after ``key:``."""
    if not rest:
        return None
    if rest[0] in "\"'":
        close = rest.find(rest[0], 1)
        if close < 0:
            return None
        return base + 1, base + close
    if rest[0] in "|>&*{[":
        return None
    value = re.split(r"\s+#", rest, maxsplit=1)[0].rstrip()
    return (base, base + len(value)) if value else None


def yaml_span(text: str, path: list[str]) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """
    Find a scalar value in a block-style YAML document by key path.

    :param text: YAML source.
    :param path: Mapping keys from the root to the value.
    :return: Start and end of the scalar, inside its quotes when quoted, or
        ``None``.
    """
    depth = 0
    parent_indent = -1
    child_indent: int | None = None
    offset = 0
    for line in text.splitlines(keepends=True):
        bare = line.rstrip("\r\n")
        line_offset = offset
        offset += len(line)
        if not bare.strip() or bare.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        match = _YAML_LINE.match(bare)
        indent = len(bare) - len(bare.lstrip())
        if indent <= parent_indent:
            if depth == 0:
                continue
            return None
        if match is None:
            continue
        if child_indent is None:
            child_indent = indent
        if indent != child_indent:
            continue
        key = match["key"].strip().strip("\"'")
        if key != path[depth]:
            continue
        if depth == len(path) - 1:
            rest = match["rest"] or ""
            return (
                _yaml_scalar(rest, line_offset + match.start("rest")) if rest else None
            )
        depth += 1
        parent_indent = indent
        child_indent = None
    return None
```

## File: src/gitversioned/errors.py

```python
"""
Errors raised by gitversioned, each mapped to a CLI exit code.

Exit codes: 1 for a failed check or nothing to release, 2 for bad usage or
configuration, 3 for a problem with the environment such as a shallow clone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

__all__ = [
    "CheckFailedError",
    "ConfigError",
    "EnvironmentProblemError",
    "GitVersionedError",
    "NothingToReleaseError",
]


class GitVersionedError(Exception):
    """
    Base class for every error gitversioned raises on purpose.

    :cvar exit_code: Process exit code the CLI uses for this error.
    """

    exit_code: int = 1


class CheckFailedError(GitVersionedError):
    """A validation failed: a title, a commit, a tag or the repository setup."""

    exit_code = 1


class NothingToReleaseError(GitVersionedError):
    """No commit since the last release justifies a new one."""

    exit_code = 1


class ConfigError(GitVersionedError):
    """The configuration or the command line is invalid."""

    exit_code = 2


class EnvironmentProblemError(GitVersionedError):
    """The environment cannot give a trustworthy answer (no git, shallow clone)."""

    exit_code = 3
```

## File: src/gitversioned/git.py

```python
"""
Every read gitversioned makes from git, plus the no-git fallbacks.

All calls go through :func:`run`, which never invokes a shell. Tag lookups peel
annotated tags to their commit, and dirty paths are reported from the repository
root so a project in a subfolder sees the same paths git does.

Example:
::
    from pathlib import Path
    from gitversioned import git

    repo = git.Repo.open(Path.cwd())
    if repo is not None:
        print(repo.head(), repo.tags_merged())
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

__all__ = [
    "ArchiveInfo",
    "Commit",
    "Repo",
    "is_ci",
    "read_archive",
    "read_sdist_version",
    "run",
]

ARCHIVE_FILE = ".git_archival.txt"
_FIELD_SEP = "\x1f"
_RECORD_SEP = "\x1e"
_STATUS_PREFIX = 3
_DESCRIBE_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<tag>.+)-(?P<distance>\d+)-g(?P<sha>[0-9a-f]+)$")


def is_ci() -> bool:
    """
    :return: True when a CI system is detected through the ``CI`` variable.
    """
    return os.environ.get("CI", "").strip().lower() not in ("", "0", "false", "no")


def run(args: list[str], cwd: Path, *, check: bool = True) -> str | None:
    """
    Run a git command and return its output.

    :param args: Arguments after ``git``.
    :param cwd: Folder to run in.
    :param check: When False, a failing command returns ``None`` instead of raising.
    :return: Standard output without the trailing newline, or ``None`` on failure
        when ``check`` is False.
    :raises subprocess.CalledProcessError: If the command fails and ``check`` is True.
    """
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603
            ["git", *args],  # noqa: S607
            cwd=cwd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=check,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
        )
    except FileNotFoundError:
        if check:
            raise
        return None
    if result.returncode != 0:
        return None
    return result.stdout.rstrip("\n")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Commit:
    """
    One commit as the changelog and the bump rules need it.

    :param sha: Full commit hash.
    :param subject: First line of the message.
    :param body: Rest of the message.
    """

    sha: str
    subject: str
    body: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ArchiveInfo:
    """
    What a ``git archive`` export file says about the exported commit.

    :param sha: Commit hash, when the file was expanded.
    :param tags: Tag names pointing at the commit or named by ``describe``.
    :param distance: Commits since the nearest tag.
    :param date: Commit date.
    """

    sha: str | None
    tags: tuple[str, ...]
    distance: int
    date: datetime | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Repo:
    """
    A git repository seen from a project folder inside it.

    :param top: Repository root.
    :param cwd: Project folder the commands run from.
    """

    top: Path
    cwd: Path

    @classmethod
    def open(cls, cwd: Path) -> Repo | None:
        """
        Open the repository containing a folder.

        :param cwd: Any folder inside the work tree.
        :return: The repository, or ``None`` when git is missing or the folder is
            not in a work tree.
        """
        if not cwd.is_dir():
            return None
        top = run(["rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], cwd, check=False)
        if not top:
            return None
        return cls(top=Path(top).resolve(), cwd=cwd.resolve())

    def git(self, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> str | None:
        """
        Run a git command from the repository root.

        :param args: Arguments after ``git``.
        :param check: When False, failure returns ``None``.
        :return: The command output.
        """
        return run(list(args), self.top, check=check)

    def head(self) -> str | None:
        """
        :return: The full hash of ``HEAD``, or ``None`` in a repository with no
            commits.
        """
        return self.git("rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD", check=False) or None

    def head_date(self) -> datetime | None:
        """
        :return: The committer date of ``HEAD`` in UTC.
        """
        stamp = self.git("log", "-1", "--format=%ct", check=False)
        if not stamp:
            return None
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(stamp), tz=timezone.utc)

    def branch(self) -> str | None:
        """
        :return: The current branch name, or ``None`` on a detached ``HEAD``.
        """
        return self.git("symbolic-ref", "--short", "-q", "HEAD", check=False) or None

    def is_shallow(self) -> bool:
        """
        :return: True when history was cut by a shallow clone.
        """
        return self.git("rev-parse", "--is-shallow-repository", check=False) == "true"

    def tags_merged(self, ref: str = "HEAD") -> dict[str, str]:
        """
        List the tags reachable from a ref with the commit each one points at.

        Annotated tags are peeled, so the hash is always a commit.

        :param ref: Ref the tags must be reachable from.
        :return: Tag name to commit hash.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "for-each-ref",
            "--merged",
            ref,
            "--format=%(refname:short)%1f%(objectname)%1f%(*objectname)",
            "refs/tags",
            check=False,
        )
        tags: dict[str, str] = {}
        for line in (out or "").splitlines():
            name, obj, peeled = (line.split(_FIELD_SEP) + ["", ""])[:3]
            tags[name] = peeled or obj
        return tags

    def all_tags(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: Every tag name in the repository.
        """
        out = self.git("tag", "--list", check=False)
        return out.splitlines() if out else []

    def distance(self, since: str | None, ref: str = "HEAD") -> int:
        """
        Count the commits on a ref after a starting point.

        :param since: Commit or tag to count from; ``None`` counts all history.
        :param ref: Ref to count to.
        :return: Number of commits.
        """
        spec = f"{since}..{ref}" if since else ref
        out = self.git("rev-list", "--count", spec, check=False)
        return int(out) if out and out.isdigit() else 0

    def commits(
        self,
        since: str | None,
        ref: str = "HEAD",
        path: Path | None = None,
        exclude: list[Path] | None = None,
    ) -> list[Commit]:
        """
        List the commits on a ref after a starting point, newest first.

        :param since: Commit or tag to start after; ``None`` lists all history.
        :param ref: Ref to list to.
        :param path: Only commits touching this folder, for a package.
        :param exclude: Folders whose commits do not count, for packages that
            carry their own tags.
        :return: The commits.
        """
        spec = f"{since}..{ref}" if since else ref
        args = ["log", f"--format=%H{_FIELD_SEP}%s{_FIELD_SEP}%b{_RECORD_SEP}", spec]
        if path is not None:
            args += ["--", str(path)]
        elif exclude:
            args += [
                "--",
                ".",
                *[f":(exclude){self.relative(item)}" for item in exclude],
            ]
        out = self.git(*args, check=False) or ""
        commits: list[Commit] = []
        for record in out.split(_RECORD_SEP):
            if not record.strip():
                continue
            sha, subject, body = (record.strip("\n").split(_FIELD_SEP) + ["", ""])[:3]
            commits.append(Commit(sha=sha, subject=subject, body=body.strip()))
        return commits

    def dirty_paths(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        List tracked files with uncommitted changes, relative to the repository root.

        Untracked files do not count, matching ``git describe --dirty``.

        :return: Paths with staged or unstaged changes.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "status", "--porcelain=v1", "--untracked-files=no", "-z", check=False
        )
        paths: list[str] = []
        entries = (out or "").split("\0")
        index = 0
        while index < len(entries):
            entry = entries[index]
            index += 1
            if len(entry) <= _STATUS_PREFIX:
                continue
            paths.append(entry[_STATUS_PREFIX:])
            if entry[0] in "RC":
                index += 1
        return paths

    def show(self, path: str, ref: str = "HEAD") -> str | None:
        """
        Read a file as committed.

        :param path: Path relative to the repository root.
        :param ref: Commit to read from.
        :return: The file text, or ``None`` when it does not exist there.
        """
        return self.git("show", f"{ref}:{path}", check=False)

    def tracked_files(self) -> list[str]:
        """
        :return: Tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored files, relative to the root.
        """
        out = self.git(
            "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard", check=False
        )
        return out.splitlines() if out else []

    def relative(self, path: Path) -> str:
        """
        Express a path relative to the repository root with forward slashes.

        :param path: Absolute path inside the work tree.
        :return: The relative path.
        """
        return path.resolve().relative_to(self.top).as_posix()


def read_archive(root: Path) -> ArchiveInfo | None:
    """
    Read a ``git archive`` export file in either supported layout.

    Both the setuptools-scm layout (``node``, ``node-date``, ``describe-name``,
    ``ref-names``) and the gitversioned layout (``commit_sha``, ``commit_date``,
    ``ref_names``) are accepted. A file that was never expanded is ignored.

    :param root: Folder holding ``.git_archival.txt``.
    :return: The archive details, or ``None`` when absent or unexpanded.
    """
    path = root / ARCHIVE_FILE
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    fields: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        key, sep, value = line.partition(":")
        if sep:
            fields[key.strip().lower().replace("_", "-")] = value.strip()
    values = {
        key: value
        for key, value in fields.items()
        if value and "$Format" not in value and not value.startswith("%")
    }
    if not values:
        return None
    sha = values.get("node") or values.get("commit-sha")
    tags, distance = _archive_tags(values)
    date: datetime | None = None
    raw_date = values.get("node-date") or values.get("commit-date")
    if raw_date:
        try:
            date = datetime.fromisoformat(raw_date).astimezone(timezone.utc)
        except ValueError:
            date = None
    if not sha and not tags:
        return None
    return ArchiveInfo(sha=sha, tags=tuple(tags), distance=distance, date=date)


def _archive_tags(values: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[list[str], int]:
```
