```python
    """Read the tag names and the distance from expanded archive fields."""
    tags: list[str] = []
    distance = 0
    describe = values.get("describe-name", "")
    match = _DESCRIBE_RE.match(describe)
    if match:
        tags.append(match["tag"])
        distance = int(match["distance"])
    elif describe:
        tags.append(describe)
    exact = [
        name.strip()[len("tag: ") :].strip()
        for name in values.get("ref-names", "").split(",")
        if name.strip().startswith("tag: ")
    ]
    if exact:
        distance = 0
    return list(dict.fromkeys(exact + tags)), distance


def read_sdist_version(root: Path) -> str | None:
    """
    Read the version recorded in an unpacked source distribution.

    :param root: Folder that may hold ``PKG-INFO``.
    :return: The ``Version`` field, or ``None``.
    """
    path = root / "PKG-INFO"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if line.startswith("Version:"):
            return line.partition(":")[2].strip() or None
        if not line.strip():
            break
    return None
```

## File: src/gitversioned/github.py

```python
"""
The GitHub side of a release, through the ``gh`` command line tool.

Nothing here is needed to resolve, stamp or check a version. The release pull
request, pull request titles for the changelog and label overrides use it, and
each caller degrades or fails with a clear message when ``gh`` is not usable.

Example:
::
    from pathlib import Path
    from gitversioned import github

    if github.available(Path.cwd()):
        print(github.pull_request(Path.cwd(), 41))
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from gitversioned import git
from gitversioned.errors import EnvironmentProblemError

__all__ = [
    "PullRequest",
    "available",
    "create_pull_request",
    "find_open_pull_request",
    "gh",
    "pull_request",
    "repo_url",
    "update_pull_request",
]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PullRequest:
    """
    The parts of a pull request gitversioned reads.

    :param number: Pull request number.
    :param title: Title.
    :param body: Description.
    :param labels: Label names.
    :param url: Web address.
    """

    number: int
    title: str
    body: str
    labels: tuple[str, ...]
    url: str = ""


def gh(args: list[str], cwd: Path, *, check: bool = True) -> str | None:
    """
    Run a ``gh`` command.

    :param args: Arguments after ``gh``.
    :param cwd: Folder to run in.
    :param check: When False, failure returns ``None`` instead of raising.
    :return: Standard output, or ``None`` on failure when ``check`` is False.
    :raises EnvironmentProblemError: If ``gh`` is missing or the command fails
        and ``check`` is True.
    """
    if shutil.which("gh") is None:
        if check:
            raise EnvironmentProblemError(
                "the GitHub CLI `gh` is not installed. Install it from "
                "https://cli.github.com to use release --pr."
            )
        return None
    result = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603
        ["gh", *args],  # noqa: S607
        cwd=cwd,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        if check:
            raise EnvironmentProblemError(
                f"gh {' '.join(args[:2])} failed: {result.stderr.strip()}"
            )
        return None
    return result.stdout.strip()


def available(cwd: Path) -> bool:
    """
    :return: True when ``gh`` is installed and signed in for this repository.
    """
    return gh(["auth", "status"], cwd, check=False) is not None


def repo_url(repo: git.Repo) -> str | None:
    """
    Work out the web address of the repository from its ``origin`` remote.

    :param repo: The repository.
    :return: An ``https://github.com/owner/name`` address, or ``None``.
    """
    remote = repo.git("remote", "get-url", "origin", check=False)
    if not remote:
        return None
    match = re.match(
        r"^(?:https?://|git@|ssh://git@)(?P<host>[^/:]+)[/:](?P<path>.+?)(?:\.git)?/?$",
        remote.strip(),
    )
    if match is None or "github" not in match["host"]:
        return None
    return f"https://{match['host']}/{match['path']}"


def _to_pull_request(data: dict[str, Any]) -> PullRequest:
    """Build a pull request from ``gh`` JSON."""
    return PullRequest(
        number=int(data["number"]),
        title=data.get("title", ""),
        body=data.get("body", "") or "",
        labels=tuple(label["name"] for label in data.get("labels", [])),
        url=data.get("url", ""),
    )


def pull_request(cwd: Path, number: int) -> PullRequest | None:
    """
    Read one pull request.

    :param cwd: Folder inside the repository.
    :param number: Pull request number.
    :return: The pull request, or ``None`` when it cannot be read.
    """
    out = gh(
        ["pr", "view", str(number), "--json", "number,title,body,labels,url"],
        cwd,
        check=False,
    )
    if not out:
        return None
    try:
        return _to_pull_request(json.loads(out))
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError):
        return None


def find_open_pull_request(cwd: Path, head: str) -> PullRequest | None:
    """
    Find the open pull request for a head branch.

    :param cwd: Folder inside the repository.
    :param head: Head branch name.
    :return: The pull request, or ``None`` when none is open.
    """
    out = gh(
        [
            "pr",
            "list",
            "--head",
            head,
            "--state",
            "open",
            "--json",
            "number,title,body,labels,url",
        ],
        cwd,
    )
    items = json.loads(out or "[]")
    return _to_pull_request(items[0]) if items else None


def create_pull_request(
    cwd: Path, *, head: str, base: str, title: str, body: str, label: str
) -> PullRequest:
    """
    Open a pull request and label it.

    :param cwd: Folder inside the repository.
    :param head: Head branch.
    :param base: Base branch.
    :param title: Title.
    :param body: Description.
    :param label: Label to add; created when missing.
    :return: The opened pull request.
    """
    gh(["label", "create", label, "--force"], cwd, check=False)
    url = gh(
        [
            "pr",
            "create",
            "--head",
            head,
            "--base",
            base,
            "--title",
            title,
            "--body",
            body,
            "--label",
            label,
        ],
        cwd,
    )
    found = find_open_pull_request(cwd, head)
    if found is not None:
        return found
    return PullRequest(number=0, title=title, body=body, labels=(label,), url=url or "")


def update_pull_request(cwd: Path, number: int, *, title: str, body: str) -> None:
    """
    Replace the title and description of a pull request.

    :param cwd: Folder inside the repository.
    :param number: Pull request number.
    :param title: New title.
    :param body: New description.
    """
    gh(["pr", "edit", str(number), "--title", title, "--body", body], cwd)
```

## File: src/gitversioned/logging.py

```python
"""
Logging setup: the standard library logger on standard error for the CLI.

As a library gitversioned logs to the ``gitversioned`` logger and adds no
handler of its own, so it stays silent until the application configures logging.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.logging import configure_logging

    configure_logging(verbosity=1)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import sys
from typing import Annotated

__all__ = ["LOGGER_NAME", "configure_logging", "logger"]

LOGGER_NAME: Annotated[str, "Name of the logger every module writes to"] = (
    "gitversioned"
)
logger: Annotated[logging.Logger, "The package logger"] = logging.getLogger(LOGGER_NAME)
logger.addHandler(logging.NullHandler())

_LEVELS = {-1: logging.ERROR, 0: logging.WARNING, 1: logging.INFO, 2: logging.DEBUG}


def configure_logging(verbosity: int = 0) -> None:
    """
    Send gitversioned's log output to standard error at the chosen level.

    :param verbosity: ``-1`` for errors only, ``0`` for warnings, ``1`` for
        information, ``2`` or more for debug output.
    """
    level = _LEVELS[max(-1, min(2, verbosity))]
    for handler in list(logger.handlers):
        if not isinstance(handler, logging.NullHandler):
            logger.removeHandler(handler)
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stderr)
    handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(levelname)-7s %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(handler)
    logger.setLevel(level)
    logger.propagate = False
```

## File: src/gitversioned/model.py

```python
"""
The version value: parsing of tag and version spellings and printing per standard.

A :class:`Version` holds the parts shared by PEP 440 and SemVer and prints itself in
either spelling, so one resolved version can be stamped into Python and non-Python
files alike.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.model import Version

    version = Version.parse("v1.3.0-rc.1")
    assert version.pep440() == "1.3.0rc1"
    assert version.semver() == "1.3.0-rc.1"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
from typing import Literal

from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError

__all__ = ["Level", "PreKind", "Standard", "Version"]

Level = Literal["major", "minor", "patch"]
PreKind = Literal["alpha", "beta", "rc"]
Standard = Literal["pep440", "semver"]

_PRE_ALIASES: dict[str, PreKind] = {
    "a": "alpha",
    "alpha": "alpha",
    "b": "beta",
    "beta": "beta",
    "rc": "rc",
    "c": "rc",
    "pre": "rc",
    "preview": "rc",
}
_PRE_PEP440: dict[str, str] = {"alpha": "a", "beta": "b", "rc": "rc"}
_PRE_ORDER: dict[str, int] = {"alpha": 0, "beta": 1, "rc": 2}

_VERSION_RE = re.compile(
    r"""
    ^v?
    (?P<major>\d+)\.(?P<minor>\d+)\.(?P<patch>\d+)
    (?:[-._]?(?P<pre>alpha|beta|preview|pre|rc|a|b|c)[-._]?(?P<pre_num>\d+)?)?
    (?:[-._]?(?P<dev_kind>dev|nightly)[-._]?(?P<dev>\d+)?)?
    (?:\+(?P<local>[0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?
    $
    """,
    re.VERBOSE | re.IGNORECASE,
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Version:
    """
    A version with the parts PEP 440 and SemVer have in common.

    :param major: Major release number.
    :param minor: Minor release number.
    :param patch: Patch release number.
    :param pre: Pre-release kind and number, such as ``("rc", 1)``.
    :param dev: Development number, normally a ``YYYYMMDD`` date.
    :param local: Local build label, normally the short commit hash.
    :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly build, which
        changes only the SemVer spelling.
    """

    major: int
    minor: int
    patch: int
    pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
    dev: int | None = None
    local: str | None = None
    nightly: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, text: str) -> Version:
        """
        Parse a version or tag spelling in PEP 440 or SemVer form.

        :param text: Text such as ``1.2.3``, ``v1.3.0-rc.1``, ``1.3.0rc1`` or
            ``1.2.1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        :return: The parsed version.
        :raises ConfigError: If the text is not a recognised version.
        """
        found = cls.try_parse(text)
        if found is None:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"not a version: {text!r}. Expected X.Y.Z with an optional "
                "pre-release such as -rc.1 or rc1."
            )
        return found

    @classmethod
    def try_parse(cls, text: str) -> Version | None:
        """
        Parse a version spelling, returning ``None`` when it does not match.

        :param text: Candidate version text.
        :return: The parsed version, or ``None``.
        """
        match = _VERSION_RE.match(text.strip())
        if match is None:
            return None
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None
        if match["pre"]:
            pre = (_PRE_ALIASES[match["pre"].lower()], int(match["pre_num"] or 0))
        dev = None
        if match["dev_kind"]:
            dev = int(match["dev"] or 0)
        return cls(
            major=int(match["major"]),
            minor=int(match["minor"]),
            patch=int(match["patch"]),
            pre=pre,
            dev=dev,
            local=match["local"],
            nightly=(match["dev_kind"] or "").lower() == "nightly",
        )

    @property
    def release(self) -> Version:
        """
        :return: The plain ``X.Y.Z`` release this version belongs to.
        """
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch)

    @property
    def is_final(self) -> bool:
        """
        :return: True for a plain ``X.Y.Z`` release.
        """
        return self.pre is None and self.dev is None

    def bump(self, level: str) -> Version:
        """
        Return the next plain release at the given level.

        :param level: Which part to raise.
        :return: A plain ``X.Y.Z`` version.
        """
        if level == "major":
            return Version(self.major + 1, 0, 0)
        if level == "minor":
            return Version(self.major, self.minor + 1, 0)
        return Version(self.major, self.minor, self.patch + 1)

    def with_parts(
        self,
        *,
        pre: tuple[str, int] | None = None,
        dev: int | None = None,
        local: str | None = None,
        nightly: bool = False,
    ) -> Version:
        """
        Return a copy with the variable parts replaced.

        :param pre: Pre-release kind and number.
        :param dev: Development number.
        :param local: Local build label.
        :param nightly: Whether the development number marks a nightly.
        :return: The new version.
        """
        return replace(self, pre=pre, dev=dev, local=local, nightly=nightly)

    def pep440(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The PEP 440 spelling, such as ``1.3.0rc1.dev20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        if self.pre is not None:
            text += f"{_PRE_PEP440[self.pre[0]]}{self.pre[1]}"
        if self.dev is not None:
            text += f".dev{self.dev}"
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def semver(self) -> str:
        """
        :return: The SemVer spelling, such as ``1.3.0-rc.1`` or
            ``1.2.1-dev.20261125+abc1234``.
        """
        text = f"{self.major}.{self.minor}.{self.patch}"
        parts: list[str] = []
        if self.pre is not None:
            parts += [self.pre[0], str(self.pre[1])]
        if self.dev is not None:
            parts += ["nightly" if self.nightly else "dev", str(self.dev)]
        if parts:
            text += "-" + ".".join(parts)
        if self.local:
            text += "+" + re.sub(r"[^0-9A-Za-z.-]", ".", self.local)
        return text

    def render(self, standard: str) -> str:
        """
        Print the version in the given standard.

        :param standard: ``pep440`` or ``semver``.
        :return: The version text.
        """
        return self.pep440() if standard == "pep440" else self.semver()

    def sort_key(self) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int, int, int]:
        """
        Return a key ordering versions the way both standards agree on.

        A development build sorts before its release, a pre-release sorts before
        the final, and a final sorts last for the same ``X.Y.Z``.

        :return: A tuple usable with ``sorted`` and ``max``.
        """
        if self.pre is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = _PRE_ORDER[self.pre[0]], self.pre[1]
        elif self.dev is not None:
            pre_rank, pre_num = -1, 0
        else:
            pre_rank, pre_num = 3, 0
        dev_rank, dev_num = (1, 0) if self.dev is None else (0, self.dev)
        return (
            self.major,
            self.minor,
            self.patch,
            pre_rank,
            pre_num,
            dev_rank,
            dev_num,
        )

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.pep440()
```

## File: src/gitversioned/release.py

```python
"""
The release flow: plan, write, pull request and tag.

A plan is computed first and changes nothing. The three stages build on it:
writing edits the changelog and the committed targets, the pull request stage
commits those edits to the release branch and opens or updates the pull request,
and the tag stage tags the merged release commit.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.config import load_config
    from gitversioned.release import plan_release

    plan = plan_release(load_config(), use_github=False)
    print(plan.version.pep440(), plan.tag)
    print(plan.section)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from gitversioned import git, github
from gitversioned.changelog import (
    Entry,
    entries_from_commits,
    insert_section,
    read_section,
    render_section,
)
from gitversioned.commits import BumpPlan, env_bump, next_version, parse_subject
from gitversioned.config import Config
from gitversioned.errors import (
    CheckFailedError,
    ConfigError,
    EnvironmentProblemError,
)
from gitversioned.logging import logger
from gitversioned.model import Version
from gitversioned.resolve import (
    Resolved,
    match_tag,
    own_tag_folders,
    release_tags,
    resolve,
    tag_name,
)
from gitversioned.targets import Change, discover, stamp

__all__ = [
    "RELEASE_BRANCH",
    "RELEASE_LABEL",
    "ReleasePlan",
    "open_release_pr",
    "package_context",
    "plan_release",
    "tag_release",
    "write_release",
]

RELEASE_BRANCH = "release/next"
RELEASE_LABEL = "release"
RC_LABEL = "release:rc"
_BUMP_LABELS = {
    "release:major": "major",
    "release:minor": "minor",
    "release:patch": "patch",
}
_RANK = {"patch": 1, "minor": 2, "major": 3}


@dataclass
class ReleasePlan:
    """
    Everything a release would do.

    :param version: Version to release.
    :param previous: Version of the latest release tag, if any.
    :param tag: Tag the release gets.
    :param level: Bump level and where it came from, for the report.
    :param section: Rendered changelog section.
    :param files: Paths the release changes, relative to the project root.
    :param entries: Changelog entries.
    :param bump: What the commits asked for.
    :param package: Package being released, when not the repository.
    :param title: Title of the release commit and pull request.
    :param branch: Release branch name.
    """

    version: Version
    previous: Version | None
    tag: str
    level: str
    section: str
    files: list[str]
    entries: list[Entry] = field(default_factory=list)
    bump: BumpPlan = field(default_factory=lambda: BumpPlan(None, ()))
    package: str | None = None
    title: str = ""
    branch: str = RELEASE_BRANCH


def package_context(config: Config, package: str | None) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """
    Work out the tag template and commit scope for the repository or a package.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param package: Package name from ``[packages]``, or ``None``.
    :return: The tag template and the folder whose commits count.
    :raises ConfigError: If the package is unknown.
    """
    if package is None:
        return config.tag, None
    if package not in config.packages:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"unknown package {package!r}. Packages: "
            f"{', '.join(config.packages) or 'none configured'}."
        )
    item = config.packages[package]
    if item.tag is None:
        return config.tag, None
    return item.tag, item.path


def _changelog_path(config: Config, package: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Return the changelog path, relative to the project root."""
    if config.changelog is False:
        return None
    if package is not None and config.packages[package].tag:
        return f"{config.packages[package].path.rstrip('/')}/CHANGELOG.md"
    return str(config.changelog)


def _require_repo(config: Config) -> git.Repo:
    """Open the repository or fail with an environment error."""
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is None or repo.head() is None:
        raise EnvironmentProblemError("a release needs a git repository with commits.")
    return repo


def _pull_requests(
    config: Config, commits: list[git.Commit], use_github: bool
) -> dict[int, github.PullRequest]:
    """Read the pull requests behind squash commits, when GitHub is reachable."""
    requests: dict[int, github.PullRequest] = {}
    if not use_github or not github.available(config.root):
        return requests
    for commit in commits:
        parsed = parse_subject(commit.subject)
        number = parsed.pr if parsed else None
        if number is None or number in requests:
            continue
        found = github.pull_request(config.root, number)
        if found is not None:
            requests[number] = found
    return requests


def _label_bump(
    commits: list[git.Commit], requests: dict[int, github.PullRequest]
) -> str | None:
    """Return the highest bump level asked for by pull request labels."""
    best: str | None = None
    for commit in commits:
        parsed = parse_subject(commit.subject)
        request = requests.get(parsed.pr) if parsed and parsed.pr else None
        for label in request.labels if request else ():
            level = _BUMP_LABELS.get(label)
            if level and (best is None or _RANK[level] > _RANK[best]):
                best = level
    return best


def _overrides(
    version: str | None,
    bump: str | None,
    labelled: str | None,
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str]:
    """
    Settle which override applies.

    :return: The explicit version or level, the bump level and where the choice
        came from, in the order VERSION, ``--bump``, environment, label, commits.
    """
    if version is not None:
        return version, bump, "VERSION"
    if bump is not None:
        return None, bump, "--bump"
    from_env = env_bump()
    if from_env:
        return from_env, None, "GITVERSIONED__BUMP"
    if labelled:
        return None, labelled, "label"
    return None, None, "commits"


def _level_text(
    resolved: Resolved, explicit: str | None, bump: str | None, source: str
) -> str:
    """Describe how the release level was chosen, for the plan report."""
    level = bump or (explicit if explicit in _RANK else None)
    if explicit and explicit not in _RANK:
        text = f"set by {source}"
    elif level:
        text = f"{level}, from {source}"
    elif resolved.base is None:
        text = "first release"
    elif resolved.base.pre is not None:
        text = f"final of {resolved.base.pep440()}"
    else:
        text = f"{resolved.plan.level}, from commits"
    if resolved.base is not None:
        text += f", from {resolved.base.pep440()}"
    return text


def _release_files(config: Config, package: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """List the files a release changes, relative to the project root."""
    files: list[str] = []
    changelog = _changelog_path(config, package)
    if changelog:
        files.append(changelog)
    root = config.root.resolve()
    files += [
        item.path.resolve().relative_to(root).as_posix()
        for item in discover(config, package=package)
        if item.commit
    ]
    return files


def plan_release(  # noqa: PLR0913
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
    use_github: bool = True,
) -> ReleasePlan:
    """
    Compute what a release would do, changing nothing.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to release exactly.
    :param bump: Level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the release a pre-release of this kind.
    :param package: Package to release instead of the repository.
    :param use_github: Read pull request titles, bodies and labels through ``gh``
        when it is available.
    :return: The plan.
    :raises NothingToReleaseError: If nothing releasable happened since the last
        release and no override is given.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If the chosen version is not newer than the last
        release.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    template, scope = package_context(config, package)
    resolved = resolve(config, tag_template=template, path_scope=scope)

    merged = repo.tags_merged()
    tags = release_tags(template, list(merged))
    finals = {name: found for name, found in tags.items() if found.is_final}
    last_final = (
        max(finals, key=lambda name: finals[name].sort_key()) if finals else None
    )
    scope_path = (config.root / scope) if scope else None
    excluded = [] if scope_path else own_tag_folders(config)
    since_final = repo.commits(
        merged[last_final] if last_final else None, path=scope_path, exclude=excluded
    )
    since_tag = repo.commits(
        merged[resolved.tag] if resolved.tag else None,
        path=scope_path,
        exclude=excluded,
    )
    requests = _pull_requests(config, since_final, use_github)
    explicit, chosen, source = _overrides(
        version, bump, _label_bump(since_tag, requests)
    )
    target = next_version(
        resolved.base,
        resolved.known,
        resolved.plan,
        fallback=Version.parse(config.fallback),
        explicit=explicit,
        bump=chosen,
        pre=pre,
    )
    if resolved.base is not None and target.sort_key() <= resolved.base.sort_key():
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"{target.pep440()} is not newer than {resolved.tag} "
            f"({resolved.base.pep440()})."
        )
    entries = entries_from_commits(since_final, requests)
    day = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    name = tag_name(template, target)
    prefix = f"release({package})" if package else "release"
    return ReleasePlan(
        version=target,
        previous=resolved.base,
        tag=name,
        level=_level_text(resolved, explicit, chosen, source),
        section=render_section(
            target, entries, day=day, repo_url=github.repo_url(repo)
        ),
        files=_release_files(config, package),
        entries=entries,
        bump=resolved.plan,
        package=package,
        title=f"{prefix}: {name}",
        branch=f"{RELEASE_BRANCH}-{package}" if package else RELEASE_BRANCH,
    )


def write_release(config: Config, plan: ReleasePlan) -> list[str]:
    """
    Apply a plan to the working tree: changelog and committed targets.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param plan: The plan to apply.
    :return: Paths that changed, relative to the project root.
    """
    changed: list[str] = []
    changelog = _changelog_path(config, plan.package)
    if changelog:
        path = config.root / changelog
        old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if path.is_file() else ""
        new = insert_section(old, plan.version, plan.section)
        if new != old:
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(new)
            changed.append(changelog)
    resolved = Resolved(
        version=plan.version, type="release", source="release", tag=plan.tag
    )
    changes: list[Change] = stamp(
        config, resolved, package=plan.package, committed_only=True
    )
    changed += [change.path for change in changes if change.written]
    return changed


def _identity(repo: git.Repo) -> list[str]:
    """Return ``-c`` options giving git an author when none is configured."""
    if repo.git("config", "user.email", check=False):
        return []
    return [
        "-c",
        "user.name=github-actions[bot]",
        "-c",
        "user.email=41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com",
    ]


def open_release_pr(
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    bump: str | None = None,
    pre: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
) -> tuple[ReleasePlan, github.PullRequest, bool]:
    """
    Open the release pull request, or update the one already open.

    The release branch is rebuilt from the current commit every time, so the pull
    request always holds exactly one commit on top of the release branch's base.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to release exactly.
    :param bump: Level that replaces the one chosen from commits.
    :param pre: Make the release a pre-release of this kind.
    :param package: Package to release instead of the repository.
    :return: The plan, the pull request and whether it was newly opened.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If the working tree has uncommitted changes.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    if not github.available(config.root):
        raise EnvironmentProblemError(
            "release --pr needs the GitHub CLI `gh`, signed in (set GH_TOKEN in CI)."
        )
    if repo.dirty_paths():
        raise CheckFailedError(
            "the working tree has uncommitted changes; commit or stash them first."
        )
    branch = f"{RELEASE_BRANCH}-{package}" if package else RELEASE_BRANCH
    existing = github.find_open_pull_request(config.root, branch)
    if pre is None and existing is not None and RC_LABEL in existing.labels:
        pre = "rc"
    plan = plan_release(config, version=version, bump=bump, pre=pre, package=package)

    start = repo.branch() or repo.head() or "HEAD"
    repo.git("checkout", "-q", "-B", plan.branch)
    try:
        changed = write_release(config, plan)
        root_in_repo = config.root.resolve().relative_to(repo.top).as_posix()
        paths = [
            path if root_in_repo == "." else f"{root_in_repo}/{path}"
            for path in changed
        ]
        if paths:
            repo.git("add", "--", *paths)
        repo.git(*_identity(repo), "commit", "-q", "--allow-empty", "-m", plan.title)
        repo.git("push", "-q", "--force", "origin", plan.branch)
    finally:
        repo.git("checkout", "-q", start, check=False)

    body = (
        f"{plan.section}\n---\n"
        f"Merging this pull request releases `{plan.tag}`. "
        f"Add the `{RC_LABEL}` label to make it a release candidate.\n"
    )
    if existing is None:
        request = github.create_pull_request(
            config.root,
            head=plan.branch,
            base=config.branch,
            title=plan.title,
            body=body,
            label=RELEASE_LABEL,
        )
        return plan, request, True
    github.update_pull_request(
        config.root, existing.number, title=plan.title, body=body
    )
    return plan, existing, False


_RELEASE_SUBJECT = re.compile(r"^release(?:\((?P<package>[^)]+)\))?: (?P<tag>\S+)")


def _released_tag(repo: git.Repo, package: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Read the tag named by the release commit at ``HEAD``, if it is one."""
    subjects = [repo.git("log", "-1", "--format=%s", "HEAD", check=False) or ""]
    second = repo.git("log", "-1", "--format=%s", "HEAD^2", check=False)
    if second:
        subjects.append(second)
    for subject in subjects:
        match = _RELEASE_SUBJECT.match(subject)
        if match and (match["package"] or None) == package:
            return match["tag"]
    return None


def tag_release(
    config: Config,
    *,
    version: str | None = None,
    package: str | None = None,
    push: bool = True,
) -> tuple[str, str, bool]:
    """
    Tag the release commit and push the tag.

    Without a version, ``HEAD`` must be the merged release commit, whose subject
    names the tag. With a version, ``HEAD`` is tagged by hand after the same
    checks.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param version: Version to tag by hand.
    :param package: Package to tag instead of the repository.
    :param push: Push the tag to ``origin`` when that remote exists.
    :return: The tag name, the tagged commit and whether the tag was pushed.
    :raises CheckFailedError: If there is nothing to tag or the tag is not newer
        than the last release.
    """
    repo = _require_repo(config)
    template, _scope = package_context(config, package)
    if version is not None:
        name = tag_name(template, Version.parse(version))
    else:
        found = _released_tag(repo, package)
        if found is None:
            raise CheckFailedError(
                "nothing to tag: HEAD is not a merged release pull request. "
                "Pass a VERSION to tag by hand."
            )
        name = found
    target = match_tag(template, name)
    if target is None:
        raise CheckFailedError(
            f"{name!r} does not follow the tag template {template!r}."
        )
    if name in repo.all_tags():
        raise CheckFailedError(f"tag {name} already exists.")
    existing = release_tags(template, repo.all_tags())
    if existing:
        latest = max(existing, key=lambda tag: existing[tag].sort_key())
        if target.sort_key() <= existing[latest].sort_key():
            raise CheckFailedError(f"{target.pep440()} is not newer than {latest}.")
    sha = repo.head() or ""
    if config.annotated:
        changelog = _changelog_path(config, package)
        message = (
            read_section(config.root / changelog, target) if changelog else None
        ) or name
        repo.git(
            *_identity(repo), "tag", "-a", name, "-m", message, "--cleanup=verbatim"
        )
    else:
        repo.git("tag", name)
    pushed = False
    if push and repo.git("remote", "get-url", "origin", check=False):
        repo.git("push", "-q", "origin", f"refs/tags/{name}")
        pushed = True
    else:
        logger.info("no origin remote; tag %s was created locally only", name)
    return name, sha, pushed
```

## File: src/gitversioned/resolve.py

```python
"""
Resolution of the version of the current checkout.

Sources are tried in a fixed order: a pinned version, git tags, the ``git archive``
export file, source distribution metadata and finally the fallback. A missing or
untrustworthy answer warns on a developer machine and fails in CI.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.config import load_config
    from gitversioned.resolve import resolve

    resolved = resolve(load_config())
    print(resolved.version.pep440(), resolved.type, resolved.source)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from gitversioned import git
from gitversioned.commits import BumpPlan, next_version, plan_bump
from gitversioned.config import Config
from gitversioned.errors import EnvironmentProblemError, NothingToReleaseError
from gitversioned.logging import logger
from gitversioned.model import Version

__all__ = [
    "BuildType",
    "Resolved",
    "match_tag",
    "own_tag_folders",
    "release_tags",
    "resolve",
    "tag_name",
]

BuildType = Literal["release", "dev", "nightly"]


_SHORT_SHA = 7


@dataclass
class Resolved:
    """
    A resolved version and how it was reached.

    :param version: The version of this checkout.
    :param type: ``release``, ``dev`` or ``nightly``.
    :param source: Where the base came from: ``pin``, ``tag``, ``archive``,
        ``sdist`` or ``fallback``.
    :param tag: The release tag the version is based on, if any.
    :param base: The version that tag carries.
    :param distance: Commits since the tag.
    :param sha: Commit hash of the checkout.
    :param date: Commit date of the checkout.
    :param dirty: Tracked paths with uncommitted changes that count.
    :param known: Every release version tagged and reachable.
    :param plan: What the commits since the tag ask for.
    :param notes: Lines for ``--explain``.
    :param warnings: Problems that did not stop resolution.
    """

    version: Version
    type: BuildType
    source: str
    tag: str | None = None
    base: Version | None = None
    distance: int = 0
    sha: str | None = None
    date: datetime | None = None
    dirty: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    known: list[Version] = field(default_factory=list)
    plan: BumpPlan = field(default_factory=lambda: BumpPlan(None, ()))
    notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)

    @property
    def short_sha(self) -> str | None:
        """
        Shorten the commit hash for the local part of a version.

        Python packaging tools read an all-digit local part as a number and drop
        its leading zeros, so a hash that would be shortened to such a value is
        lengthened until it holds a letter.

        :return: At least the first seven characters of the commit hash.
        """
        if not self.sha:
            return None
        length = _SHORT_SHA
        while (
            length < len(self.sha)
            and self.sha[:length].isdigit()
            and self.sha.startswith("0")
        ):
            length += 1
        return self.sha[:length]


def tag_name(template: str, version: Version) -> str:
    """
    Build a tag name from a template.

    :param template: Tag template containing ``{version}``.
    :param version: Version to name; spelled as SemVer.
    :return: The tag name.
    """
    return template.replace("{version}", version.semver())


def match_tag(template: str, name: str) -> Version | None:
    """
    Read the version out of a tag name that follows a template.

    Both pre-release spellings are accepted, so ``v1.3.0-rc.1`` and ``v1.3.0rc1``
    give the same version.

    :param template: Tag template containing ``{version}``.
    :param name: Tag name to test.
    :return: The version, or ``None`` when the tag does not follow the template.
    """
    prefix, _, suffix = template.partition("{version}")
    if not name.startswith(prefix) or not name.endswith(suffix):
        return None
    body = name[len(prefix) : len(name) - len(suffix) if suffix else None]
    if not body or not body[0].isdigit():
        return None
    version = Version.try_parse(body)
    if version is None or version.dev is not None or version.local:
        return None
    return version


def release_tags(template: str, names: list[str]) -> dict[str, Version]:
    """
    Keep the tag names that are release tags for a template.

    :param template: Tag template containing ``{version}``.
    :param names: Tag names to filter.
    :return: Tag name to version.
    """
    found: dict[str, Version] = {}
    for name in names:
        version = match_tag(template, name)
        if version is not None:
            found[name] = version
    return found


def own_tag_folders(config: Config) -> list[Path]:
    """
    List the folders of packages that carry their own tags.

    Commits that only touch these folders belong to the package's releases, not
    to the repository's.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :return: Absolute package folders.
    """
    return [
        (config.root / item.path).resolve()
        for item in config.packages.values()
        if item.tag
    ]


def _problem(message: str, warnings: list[str]) -> None:
    """Fail in CI, warn elsewhere."""
    if git.is_ci():
        raise EnvironmentProblemError(message)
    logger.warning(message)
    warnings.append(message)


def _shape(
    config: Config,
    resolved: Resolved,
    build_type: BuildType,
    base_is_release: bool,
) -> Version:
    """Turn the base into a development or nightly version."""
    base = resolved.base or Version.parse(config.fallback)
    rule = config.nightly if build_type == "nightly" else config.dev
    if not base_is_release or base.pre is not None:
        target = base.release
    elif rule == "next":
        try:
            target = next_version(base, resolved.known, resolved.plan, fallback=base)
        except NothingToReleaseError:
            target = base.bump("patch")
    else:
        target = base.bump(rule)
    stamp = resolved.date if config.date == "commit" and resolved.date else None
    stamp = stamp or datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)
    number = int(stamp.strftime("%Y%m%d"))
    if build_type == "nightly":
        return target.with_parts(dev=number, nightly=True)
    local: str | None = None
    if config.local:
        parts = [
            part
            for part in (resolved.short_sha, "dirty" if resolved.dirty else None)
            if part
        ]
        local = ".".join(parts) or None
    return target.with_parts(dev=number, local=local)


def resolve(
    config: Config,
    *,
    pin: str | None = None,
    build_type: BuildType | None = None,
    tag_template: str | None = None,
    path_scope: str | None = None,
) -> Resolved:
    """
    Resolve the version of the current checkout.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param pin: A version to use as is, skipping git.
    :param build_type: Force ``release``, ``dev`` or ``nightly``; by default a
        clean tagged ``HEAD`` is a release and anything else a development build.
    :param tag_template: Tag template to use instead of the configured one, for a
        package with its own tags.
    :param path_scope: Folder, relative to the project root, whose commits count;
        used for a package with its own tags.
    :return: The resolved version and how it was reached.
    :raises EnvironmentProblemError: In CI, when no trustworthy version exists.
    """
    template = tag_template or config.tag
    pinned = pin or (config.version if config.version != "auto" else None)
    if pinned:
        version = Version.parse(pinned)
        kind: BuildType = "release"
        if version.dev is not None:
            kind = "nightly" if version.nightly else "dev"
        return Resolved(
            version=version, type=kind, source="pin", notes=[f"pinned to {pinned}"]
        )

    warnings: list[str] = []
    fallback = Version.parse(config.fallback)
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is not None and repo.head() is None:
        repo = None
    if repo is None:
        return _resolve_without_git(config, template, build_type, fallback, warnings)

    return _resolve_with_git(
        config,
        repo=repo,
        template=template,
        build_type=build_type,
        path_scope=path_scope,
        fallback=fallback,
        warnings=warnings,
    )


def _resolve_with_git(  # noqa: PLR0913
    config: Config,
    *,
    repo: git.Repo,
    template: str,
    build_type: BuildType | None,
    path_scope: str | None,
    fallback: Version,
    warnings: list[str],
) -> Resolved:
    """Resolve from the release tags reachable from ``HEAD``."""
    merged = repo.tags_merged()
    tags = release_tags(template, list(merged))
    resolved = Resolved(
        version=fallback,
        type="dev",
        source="tag" if tags else "fallback",
        sha=repo.head(),
        date=repo.head_date(),
        known=list(release_tags(template, repo.all_tags()).values()),
        warnings=warnings,
    )
    scope = (config.root / path_scope) if path_scope else None
    excluded = [] if scope else own_tag_folders(config)
    since: str | None = None
    if tags:
        best = max(tags, key=lambda name: tags[name].sort_key())
        resolved.tag = best
        resolved.base = tags[best]
        since = merged[best]
        resolved.notes.append(f"base {tags[best].pep440()} from tag {best}")
    elif repo.is_shallow():
        _problem(
            "shallow clone with no release tags reachable, so the version cannot "
            "be trusted. Fetch full history (fetch-depth: 0 on actions/checkout).",
            warnings,
        )
    else:
        message = (
            f"no release tags match {template!r}; using fallback {fallback.pep440()}."
        )
        logger.info(message)
        resolved.notes.append(message)
    commits = repo.commits(since, path=scope, exclude=excluded)
    resolved.distance = len(commits)
    resolved.plan = plan_bump(commits)

    resolved.dirty = _counted_dirty(config, repo)
    at_tag = resolved.base is not None and resolved.distance == 0 and not resolved.dirty
    kind: BuildType = build_type or ("release" if at_tag else "dev")
    resolved.type = kind
    if kind != "release":
        resolved.version = _shape(config, resolved, kind, base_is_release=bool(tags))
    elif at_tag and resolved.base is not None:
        resolved.version = resolved.base
    else:
        try:
            resolved.version = next_version(
                resolved.base, resolved.known, resolved.plan, fallback=fallback
            )
        except NothingToReleaseError:
            resolved.version = (resolved.base or fallback).release
    return resolved


def _counted_dirty(config: Config, repo: git.Repo) -> list[str]:
    """Return the dirty paths that are not just gitversioned's own stamping."""
    dirty = repo.dirty_paths()
    if not dirty:
        return []
    from gitversioned.targets import only_version_changed  # noqa: PLC0415

    return [path for path in dirty if not only_version_changed(config, repo, path)]


def _resolve_without_git(
    config: Config,
    template: str,
    build_type: BuildType | None,
    fallback: Version,
    warnings: list[str],
) -> Resolved:
    """Resolve from the archive file, sdist metadata or the fallback."""
    archive = git.read_archive(config.root)
    if archive is not None:
        tags = release_tags(template, list(archive.tags))
        resolved = Resolved(
            version=fallback,
            type="dev",
            source="archive",
            sha=archive.sha,
            date=archive.date,
            distance=archive.distance,
            warnings=warnings,
        )
        if tags:
            best = max(tags, key=lambda name: tags[name].sort_key())
            resolved.tag = best
            resolved.base = tags[best]
            resolved.known = list(tags.values())
            resolved.notes.append(
                f"base {tags[best].pep440()} from {git.ARCHIVE_FILE} ({best})"
            )
        at_tag = resolved.base is not None and resolved.distance == 0
        kind = build_type or ("release" if at_tag else "dev")
        resolved.type = kind
        if kind == "release" and resolved.base is not None:
            resolved.version = resolved.base
        else:
            if kind == "release":
                kind = resolved.type = "dev"
            resolved.version = _shape(
                config, resolved, kind, base_is_release=bool(tags)
            )
        return resolved

    sdist = git.read_sdist_version(config.root)
    if sdist and Version.try_parse(sdist) is not None:
        version = Version.parse(sdist)
        kind = (
            "release"
            if version.dev is None
            else ("nightly" if version.nightly else "dev")
        )
        return Resolved(
            version=version,
            type=kind,
            source="sdist",
            notes=[f"version {sdist} from PKG-INFO"],
            warnings=warnings,
        )

    _problem(
        "no git repository, archive file or package metadata found, so the "
        f"version cannot be resolved; using fallback {fallback.pep440()}. "
        "Set GITVERSIONED__VERSION to pin one.",
        warnings,
    )
    resolved = Resolved(
        version=fallback, type="dev", source="fallback", warnings=warnings
    )
    resolved.version = _shape(config, resolved, "dev", base_is_release=False)
    return resolved
```

## File: src/gitversioned/scaffold.py

```python
"""
The optional ``init`` step: the archive file and build backend wiring.

Every edit appends to a file or creates a new one; nothing existing is rewritten.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.config import load_config
    from gitversioned.scaffold import scaffold

    for action, path, detail in scaffold(load_config()):
        print(action, path, detail)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from gitversioned import git
from gitversioned.config import Config

__all__ = ["ARCHIVE_TEMPLATE", "scaffold"]

ARCHIVE_TEMPLATE = (
    "node: $Format:%H$\n"
    "node-date: $Format:%cI$\n"
    "describe-name: $Format:%(describe:tags=true,match=*[0-9]*)$\n"
    "ref-names: $Format:%D$\n"
)
_ATTRIBUTE_LINE = f"{git.ARCHIVE_FILE}  export-subst\n"


def _append(path, text: str) -> None:  # noqa: ANN001
    """Append text to a file, adding a newline first when the file lacks one."""
    old = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if path.is_file() else ""
    joiner = "" if not old or old.endswith("\n") else "\n"
    with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        handle.write(old + joiner + text)


def scaffold(config: Config) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
    """
    Set up the files a repository needs for versions to survive without git.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :return: One ``(action, path, detail)`` row per step, where the action is
        ``wrote``, ``edit`` or ``ok``.
    """
    actions: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
    root = config.root
    archive = root / git.ARCHIVE_FILE
    if archive.is_file():
        actions.append(("ok", git.ARCHIVE_FILE, "already present"))
    else:
        archive.write_text(ARCHIVE_TEMPLATE, encoding="utf-8")
        actions.append(("wrote", git.ARCHIVE_FILE, ""))
    attributes = root / ".gitattributes"
    current = attributes.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if attributes.is_file() else ""
    if git.ARCHIVE_FILE in current and "export-subst" in current:
        actions.append(("ok", ".gitattributes", "already marks the archive file"))
    else:
        _append(attributes, _ATTRIBUTE_LINE)
        actions.append(("edit", ".gitattributes", f"+ {_ATTRIBUTE_LINE.strip()}"))
    pyproject = root / "pyproject.toml"
    if pyproject.is_file():
        text = pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if (
            "hatchling" in text
            and "[tool.hatch.version]" not in text
            and "dynamic" in text
        ):
            _append(pyproject, '\n[tool.hatch.version]\nsource = "gitversioned"\n')
            actions.append(
                (
                    "edit",
                    "pyproject.toml",
                    '+ [tool.hatch.version] source = "gitversioned"',
                )
            )
    return actions
```

## File: src/gitversioned/targets.py

```python
"""
The files gitversioned stamps: discovery, scoped edits and the generated module.

Every target except the generated ``version.py`` is changed by replacing only the
version value in place. Discovery finds the usual manifests; listed targets add
files it cannot know about.

Example:
::
    from gitversioned.config import load_config
    from gitversioned.resolve import resolve
    from gitversioned.targets import stamp

    config = load_config()
    for change in stamp(config, resolve(config), dry_run=True):
        print(change.path, change.new)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import difflib
import re
import sys
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from gitversioned import git
from gitversioned.config import Config, TargetConfig
from gitversioned.editors import json_span, toml_span, toml_table_spans, yaml_span
from gitversioned.errors import ConfigError
from gitversioned.model import Standard
from gitversioned.resolve import Resolved

if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):
    import tomllib
else:  # pragma: no cover
    import tomli as tomllib

__all__ = [
    "Change",
    "Span",
    "Target",
    "discover",
    "only_version_changed",
    "render_version_module",
    "stamp",
]

_SKIP_DIRS = {
    "node_modules",
    "target",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "dist",
    "build",
    ".git",
    "site",
    "examples",
    "tests",
    "test",
    "testdata",
    "fixtures",
    "vendor",
    "third_party",
}
_DOCKER_LABEL = re.compile(
    r"""org\.opencontainers\.image\.version\s*=\s*(?P<q>["']?)(?P<value>[^"'\s\\]+)(?P=q)"""
)
_CARGO_DEP_TABLE = re.compile(r"(^|\.)(dev-|build-)?dependencies$")
_INLINE_VERSION = re.compile(r"""\bversion\s*=\s*(?P<q>["'])(?P<value>[^"']*)(?P=q)""")
_INLINE_PATH = re.compile(r"\bpath\s*=")
_LOCK_ENTRY = re.compile(
    r'\[\[package\]\]\s*\nname = "(?P<name>[^"]+)"\s*\nversion = "(?P<value>[^"]+)"'
)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Span:
    """
    One value to replace inside a file.

    :param kind: ``version`` for a version, ``req`` for a dependency requirement
        whose operator is kept, ``date`` for a release date.
    :param start: First character of the value.
    :param end: One past the last character.
    """

    kind: str
    start: int
    end: int


def _no_spans(text: str) -> list[Span]:  # noqa: ARG001
    """Locate nothing; the default for a generated file."""
    return []


@dataclass
class Target:
    """
    A file that carries the version.

    :param path: Absolute path of the file.
    :param kind: Handler name such as ``cargo``, ``npm`` or ``python``.
    :param standard: Spelling the file expects.
    :param commit: Whether the release pull request commits the file.
    :param locate: Finds the values to replace in the file's text.
    :param generated: True when the whole file is written from the template.
    """

    path: Path
    kind: str
    standard: Standard
    commit: bool
    locate: Callable[[str], list[Span]] = field(default=_no_spans, repr=False)
    generated: bool = False

    def current(self, text: str) -> str | None:
        """
        Read the version the file holds now.

        :param text: File content.
        :return: The first version value found, or ``None``.
        """
        for span in self.locate(text):
            if span.kind == "version":
                return text[span.start : span.end]
        return None

    def apply(self, text: str, values: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        """
        Replace each located value, leaving the rest of the text untouched.

        :param text: File content.
        :param values: Replacement per span kind.
        :return: The new content.
        """
        for span in sorted(
            self.locate(text), key=lambda item: item.start, reverse=True
        ):
            new = values.get(span.kind)
            if new is None:
                continue
            if span.kind == "req":
                operator = re.match(r"^[\^~=<>\s]*", text[span.start : span.end])
                new = (operator.group(0) if operator else "") + new
            text = text[: span.start] + new + text[span.end :]
        return text


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Change:
    """
    The result of stamping one target.

    :param path: Path relative to the project root.
    :param old: Version the file held, when it had one.
    :param new: Version written.
    :param diff: Unified diff of the edit; empty when nothing changed.
    :param commit: Whether the release pull request commits the file.
    :param written: True when the file was changed on disk.
    """

    path: str
    old: str | None
    new: str
    diff: str
    commit: bool
    written: bool


def _spans(kind: str, *found: tuple[int, int] | None) -> list[Span]:
    """Wrap raw spans, dropping the ones that were not found."""
    return [Span(kind, span[0], span[1]) for span in found if span is not None]


def _cargo_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate the package version and the versions of path dependencies."""
    spans = _spans(
        "version",
        toml_span(text, ["package", "version"]),
        toml_span(text, ["workspace", "package", "version"]),
    )
    for name, start, end in toml_table_spans(text):
        parent, _, leaf = name.rpartition(".")
        if _CARGO_DEP_TABLE.search(name):
            offset = start
            for line in text[start:end].splitlines(keepends=True):
                match = _INLINE_VERSION.search(line)
                if match and _INLINE_PATH.search(line):
                    spans.append(
                        Span(
                            "req",
                            offset + match.start("value"),
                            offset + match.end("value"),
                        )
                    )
                offset += len(line)
        elif leaf and _CARGO_DEP_TABLE.search(parent):
            body = text[start:end]
            match = re.search(
                r"""(?m)^\s*version\s*=\s*(["'])(?P<value>[^"']*)\1""", body
            )
            if match and re.search(r"(?m)^\s*path\s*=", body):
                spans.append(
                    Span(
                        "req", start + match.start("value"), start + match.end("value")
                    )
                )
    return spans


def _lock_locate(names: set[str]) -> Callable[[str], list[Span]]:
    """Build a locator for the lock entries of the workspace's own crates."""

    def locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
        return [
            Span("version", match.start("value"), match.end("value"))
            for match in _LOCK_ENTRY.finditer(text)
            if match["name"] in names
        ]

    return locate


def _keyed_locate(path: Path, key: str) -> Callable[[str], list[Span]]:
    """Build a locator for a dotted key in a TOML, JSON or YAML file."""
    parts = key.split(".")
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".toml":
        return lambda text: _spans("version", toml_span(text, parts))
    if suffix == ".json":
        return lambda text: _spans("version", json_span(text, parts))
    if suffix in (".yaml", ".yml", ".cff"):
        return lambda text: _spans("version", yaml_span(text, parts))
    raise ConfigError(
        f"target {path.name}: `key` works for .toml, .json, .yaml and .yml files. "
        "Use `pattern` for other files."
    )


def _pattern_locate(path: Path, pattern: str) -> Callable[[str], list[Span]]:
    """Build a locator from a regular expression with a ``version`` group."""
    try:
        compiled = re.compile(pattern, re.MULTILINE)
    except re.error as error:
        raise ConfigError(f"target {path.name}: invalid pattern: {error}") from error
    if "version" not in compiled.groupindex:
        raise ConfigError(f"target {path.name}: pattern needs a (?P<version>...) group")
    return lambda text: [
        Span("version", match.start("version"), match.end("version"))
        for match in compiled.finditer(text)
    ]


def _pyproject_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate a static ``[project] version``."""
    return _spans("version", toml_span(text, ["project", "version"]))


def _npm_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate the top-level ``version`` of a package.json file."""
    return _spans("version", json_span(text, ["version"]))


def _tauri_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate the version of a Tauri config, in either schema."""
    return _spans("version", json_span(text, ["version"])) or _spans(
        "version", json_span(text, ["package", "version"])
    )


def _helm_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate the chart version and the application version."""
    return _spans(
        "version", yaml_span(text, ["version"]), yaml_span(text, ["appVersion"])
    )


def _citation_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate the version and the release date of a citation file."""
    return _spans("version", yaml_span(text, ["version"])) + _spans(
        "date", yaml_span(text, ["date-released"])
    )


def _docker_locate(text: str) -> list[Span]:
    """Locate a literal OCI version label, skipping build argument references."""
    return [
        Span("version", match.start("value"), match.end("value"))
        for match in _DOCKER_LABEL.finditer(text)
        if not match["value"].startswith("$")
    ]


_NAMED: dict[str, tuple[str, Standard, Callable[[str], list[Span]]]] = {
    "pyproject.toml": ("pyproject", "pep440", _pyproject_locate),
    "Cargo.toml": ("cargo", "semver", _cargo_locate),
    "package.json": ("npm", "semver", _npm_locate),
    "tauri.conf.json": ("tauri", "semver", _tauri_locate),
    "Chart.yaml": ("helm", "semver", _helm_locate),
    "CITATION.cff": ("citation", "semver", _citation_locate),
}


def _is_dockerfile(name: str) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a file name is a Dockerfile."""
    return (
        name == "Dockerfile"
        or name.startswith("Dockerfile.")
        or name.endswith(".Dockerfile")
    )


def _by_name(path: Path) -> Target | None:
    """Build the target for a file recognised by its name."""
    if _is_dockerfile(path.name):
        return Target(path, "dockerfile", "semver", True, _docker_locate)
    found = _NAMED.get(path.name)
    if found is None:
        return None
    kind, standard, locate = found
    return Target(path, kind, standard, True, locate)


def _python_module(pyproject: Path) -> Path | None:
    """Return where the generated ``version.py`` goes for a dynamic project."""
    try:
        data = tomllib.loads(pyproject.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, tomllib.TOMLDecodeError):
        return None
    project = data.get("project", {})
    build = data.get("build-system", {})
    uses_plugin = str(build.get("build-backend", "")).startswith("gitversioned") or any(
        re.match(r"^gitversioned\b", str(item).strip())
        for item in build.get("requires", [])
    )
    if not uses_plugin:
        return None
    if "version" not in project.get("dynamic", []) or not project.get("name"):
        return None
    package = re.sub(r"[-.]+", "_", str(project["name"])).lower()
    for base in (
        pyproject.parent / "src",
        pyproject.parent,
        pyproject.parent / "python",
    ):
        if (base / package).is_dir():
            return base / package / "version.py"
    return None


def _listed(config: Config, entry: TargetConfig) -> Target:
    """Build the target for a ``[[targets]]`` entry."""
    path = (config.root / entry.path).resolve()
    if entry.pattern:
        target = Target(
            path, "pattern", "semver", True, _pattern_locate(path, entry.pattern)
        )
    elif entry.key:
        target = Target(path, "key", "semver", True, _keyed_locate(path, entry.key))
    else:
        named = _by_name(path)
        if named is None:
            raise ConfigError(
                f"target {entry.path}: unknown file type. Add `key` or `pattern`."
            )
        target = named
    if path.suffix == ".py" or path.name == "pyproject.toml":
        target.standard = "pep440"
    if entry.commit is not None:
        target.commit = entry.commit
    return target


def _candidates(config: Config, base: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """List the files discovery should look at under a folder."""
    repo = git.Repo.open(config.root)
    if repo is not None:
        files = [repo.top / name for name in repo.tracked_files()]
    else:
        files = [path for path in base.rglob("*") if path.is_file()]
    found: list[Path] = []
    for path in files:
        try:
            relative = path.resolve().relative_to(base.resolve())
        except ValueError:
            continue
        if _SKIP_DIRS.intersection(relative.parts[:-1]):
            continue
        found.append(base / relative)
    return sorted(found)


def _search_scope(config: Config, package: str | None) -> tuple[Path, list[Path]]:
    """Return the folder to search and the folders to leave out."""
    root = config.root.resolve()
    if package is None:
        return root, [
            (root / item.path).resolve()
            for item in config.packages.values()
            if item.tag
        ]
    if package not in config.packages:
        raise ConfigError(
            f"unknown package {package!r}. Packages: "
            f"{', '.join(config.packages) or 'none configured'}."
        )
    return (root / config.packages[package].path).resolve(), []


def _within(path: Path, base: Path, excluded: list[Path]) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a path is inside the search folder and not left out."""
    resolved = path.resolve()
    if any(resolved == folder or folder in resolved.parents for folder in excluded):
        return False
    return resolved == base or base in resolved.parents


def _named_target(path: Path, base: Path) -> Target | None:
    """Build the target for a discovered file that already holds a version."""
    root_only = path.name == "CITATION.cff" or "Dockerfile" in path.name
    if root_only and path.parent.resolve() != base:
        return None
    target = _by_name(path)
    if target is None:
        return None
    try:
        text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
        return None
    return target if target.current(text) is not None else None


def _discovered(paths: list[Path], base: Path) -> list[Target]:
    """Build the targets found by file name among candidate paths."""
    targets: list[Target] = []
    crate_names: set[str] = set()
    lock_dirs: list[Path] = []
    for path in paths:
        if path.name == "Cargo.toml":
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            name_span = toml_span(text, ["package", "name"])
            if name_span:
                crate_names.add(text[name_span[0] : name_span[1]])
            if (path.parent / "Cargo.lock").is_file():
                lock_dirs.append(path.parent)
        if path.name == "pyproject.toml":
            module = _python_module(path)
            if module is not None:
                targets.append(
                    Target(module, "python", "pep440", False, generated=True)
                )
        target = _named_target(path, base)
        if target is not None:
            targets.append(target)
    if crate_names and any(target.kind == "cargo" for target in targets):
        targets.extend(
            Target(
                folder / "Cargo.lock",
                "cargo-lock",
                "semver",
                True,
                _lock_locate(crate_names),
            )
            for folder in lock_dirs
        )
    return targets


def discover(config: Config, *, package: str | None = None) -> list[Target]:
    """
    Find every target of the project or of one package.

    Folders of packages that carry their own tag are left out of the repository's
    targets, and are the only folders searched when that package is asked for.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param package: Name of a package from ``[packages]`` to limit the search to.
    :return: The targets, discovered ones first, listed ones after.
    :raises ConfigError: If the package is unknown or a listed target is invalid.
    """
    base, excluded = _search_scope(config, package)
    paths = [
        path for path in _candidates(config, base) if _within(path, base, excluded)
    ]
    targets = _discovered(paths, base)
    for entry in config.targets:
        listed = _listed(config, entry)
        if not _within(listed.path, base, excluded):
            continue
        targets = [
            item for item in targets if item.path.resolve() != listed.path.resolve()
        ]
        targets.append(listed)
    return targets


def render_version_module(resolved: Resolved) -> str:
    """
    Render the generated ``version.py`` for a resolved version.

    The module carries the version and git metadata only, so two builds of the
    same commit produce the same file.

    :param resolved: The resolved version.
    :return: Python source.
    """
    version = resolved.version
    parts: list[object] = [version.major, version.minor, version.patch]
    if version.pre is not None:
        parts.append(f"{version.pre[0]}{version.pre[1]}")
    if version.dev is not None:
        parts.append(f"dev{version.dev}")
    if version.local:
        parts.append(version.local)
    date = resolved.date.isoformat() if resolved.date else None
    return (
        '"""Version information generated by gitversioned. Do not edit or commit."""\n'
        "\n"
        "from __future__ import annotations\n"
        "\n"
        "__all__ = [\n"
        '    "__commit__",\n'
        '    "__commit_date__",\n'
        '    "__distance__",\n'
        '    "__tag__",\n'
        '    "__version__",\n'
        '    "__version_semver__",\n'
        '    "__version_tuple__",\n'
        '    "version",\n'
        '    "version_tuple",\n'
        "]\n"
        "\n"
        f"__version__ = version = {version.pep440()!r}\n"
        f"__version_semver__ = {version.semver()!r}\n"
        f"__version_tuple__ = version_tuple = {tuple(parts)!r}\n"
        f"__tag__ = {resolved.tag!r}\n"
        f"__distance__ = {resolved.distance!r}\n"
        f"__commit__ = {resolved.sha!r}\n"
        f"__commit_date__ = {date!r}\n"
    ).replace("'", '"')


def _values(target: Target, resolved: Resolved) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Build the replacement values for a target."""
    rendered = resolved.version.render(target.standard)
    values = {"version": rendered, "req": rendered}
    if resolved.type == "release":
        day = datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc)
        values["date"] = day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    return values


def stamp(
    config: Config,
    resolved: Resolved,
    *,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    package: str | None = None,
    committed_only: bool = False,
    generated_only: bool = False,
) -> list[Change]:
    """
    Write the resolved version into every target.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param resolved: The version to write.
    :param dry_run: Compute the changes and diffs without touching any file.
    :param package: Limit the work to one package from ``[packages]``.
    :param committed_only: Skip targets the release pull request does not commit.
    :param generated_only: Write only the generated ``version.py`` files, as a
        build backend does.
    :return: One change per target, in discovery order.
    """
    changes: list[Change] = []
    for target in discover(config, package=package):
        if committed_only and not target.commit:
            continue
        if generated_only and not target.generated:
            continue
        relative = _relative(target.path, config.root)
        rendered = resolved.version.render(target.standard)
        old_text = _read_exact(target.path) if target.path.is_file() else ""
        if target.generated:
            old = _generated_version(old_text)
            new_text = render_version_module(resolved)
        else:
            old = target.current(old_text)
            new_text = target.apply(old_text, _values(target, resolved))
        diff = "".join(
            difflib.unified_diff(
                old_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                new_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
                f"a/{relative}",
                f"b/{relative}",
            )
        )
        changed = new_text != old_text
        if changed and not dry_run:
            target.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with target.path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(new_text)
        changes.append(
            Change(
                relative, old, rendered, diff, target.commit, changed and not dry_run
            )
        )
    return changes


def _read_exact(path: Path) -> str:
    """Read a file without translating its line endings."""
    with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
        return handle.read()


def _generated_version(text: str) -> str | None:
    """Read the version out of a generated module."""
    match = re.search(
        r"""(?m)^__version__\s*=\s*(?:version\s*=\s*)?["']([^"']+)["']""", text
    )
    return match.group(1) if match else None


def _relative(path: Path, root: Path) -> str:
    """Express a path relative to the project root when it is inside it."""
    try:
        return path.resolve().relative_to(root.resolve()).as_posix()
    except ValueError:
        return path.as_posix()


def _same_but_for_spans(target: Target, head: str, work: str) -> bool:
    """Tell whether two versions of a file differ only inside located values."""
    head_spans = sorted(target.locate(head), key=lambda item: item.start)
    work_spans = sorted(target.locate(work), key=lambda item: item.start)
    if len(head_spans) != len(work_spans) or not head_spans:
        return False
    rebuilt = head
    for head_span, work_span in reversed(
        list(zip(head_spans, work_spans, strict=True))
    ):
        rebuilt = (
            rebuilt[: head_span.start]
            + work[work_span.start : work_span.end]
            + rebuilt[head_span.end :]
        )
    return rebuilt.replace("\r\n", "\n").rstrip("\n") == work.replace(
        "\r\n", "\n"
    ).rstrip("\n")


def only_version_changed(config: Config, repo: git.Repo, path: str) -> bool:
    """
    Tell whether a dirty file differs from ``HEAD`` only by stamped values.

    This is what keeps a build from making its own tree dirty: a manifest whose
    only change is the version gitversioned wrote does not count.

    :param config: The loaded configuration.
    :param repo: The repository.
    :param path: Dirty path relative to the repository root.
    :return: True when the change is only gitversioned's own stamping.
    """
    absolute = (repo.top / path).resolve()
    try:
        targets = discover(config)
        for name in config.packages:
            targets += discover(config, package=name)
    except ConfigError:
        return False
    target = next((item for item in targets if item.path.resolve() == absolute), None)
    if target is None:
        return False
    if target.generated:
        return True
    head = repo.show(path)
    if head is None or not absolute.is_file():
        return False
    return _same_but_for_spans(target, head, _read_exact(absolute))
```

## File: src/gitversioned/plugins/__init__.py

```python
"""
Build backend integrations: Hatchling, setuptools and Maturin.

Each integration resolves the version once and writes the generated
``version.py``, so a build needs no gitversioned settings at all.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from gitversioned.config import load_config
from gitversioned.resolve import Resolved, resolve
from gitversioned.targets import Change, stamp

__all__ = ["resolve_for_build"]


def resolve_for_build(
    root: Path | str, *, write: bool = True
) -> tuple[Resolved, list[Change]]:
    """
    Resolve the version for a build and write the generated module.

    :param root: Project folder being built.
    :param write: Write the generated ``version.py`` when the project has one.
    :return: The resolved version and the files written.
    """
    config = load_config(Path(root))
    resolved = resolve(config)
    changes: list[Change] = []
    if write:
        changes = [
            change
            for change in stamp(config, resolved, generated_only=True)
            if change.written or not change.diff
        ]
    return resolved, changes
```

## File: src/gitversioned/plugins/hatchling.py

```python
"""
Hatchling integration: a version source and a build hook.

Example:
::
    [build-system]
    requires = ["hatchling", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
    build-backend = "hatchling.build"

    [tool.hatch.version]
    source = "gitversioned"

    [tool.hatch.build.hooks.gitversioned]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from hatchling.builders.hooks.plugin.interface import BuildHookInterface
from hatchling.plugin import hookimpl
from hatchling.version.source.plugin.interface import VersionSourceInterface

from gitversioned.plugins import resolve_for_build

__all__ = [
    "GitVersionedBuildHook",
    "GitVersionedVersionSource",
    "hatch_register_build_hook",
    "hatch_register_version_source",
]


class GitVersionedVersionSource(VersionSourceInterface):
    """Give Hatchling the version resolved from git and write ``version.py``."""

    PLUGIN_NAME = "gitversioned"

    def get_version_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """
        :return: The version in PEP 440 form under the ``version`` key.
        """
        resolved, _changes = resolve_for_build(self.root)
        return {"version": resolved.version.pep440()}

    def set_version(self, version: str, version_data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        """Refuse to set a version, since tags are the only source of truth."""
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "gitversioned reads versions from git tags; create a tag instead."
        )


class GitVersionedBuildHook(BuildHookInterface):
    """Ship the generated ``version.py`` even when git ignores it."""

    PLUGIN_NAME = "gitversioned"

    def initialize(self, version: str, build_data: dict[str, Any]) -> None:  # noqa: ARG002
        """
        Write the generated module and add it to the build as an artifact.

        :param version: Build version label passed by Hatchling.
        :param build_data: Mutable build data; ``artifacts`` is extended.
        """
        _resolved, changes = resolve_for_build(self.root)
        artifacts = build_data.setdefault("artifacts", [])
        for change in changes:
            if change.path not in artifacts:
                artifacts.append(change.path)


@hookimpl
def hatch_register_version_source() -> type[VersionSourceInterface]:
    """Register the version source with Hatchling."""
    return GitVersionedVersionSource


@hookimpl
def hatch_register_build_hook() -> type[BuildHookInterface]:
    """Register the build hook with Hatchling."""
    return GitVersionedBuildHook
```

## File: src/gitversioned/plugins/maturin.py

```python
"""
Maturin integration: a PEP 517 backend that stamps ``Cargo.toml`` and delegates.

Maturin reads the version from ``Cargo.toml``, so this backend writes the
resolved version there for the length of the build and puts the files back
afterwards.

Example:
::
    [build-system]
    requires = ["maturin>=1.0,<2.0", "gitversioned>=0.4"]
    build-backend = "gitversioned.plugins.maturin"
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
from collections.abc import Generator
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from gitversioned.config import load_config
from gitversioned.resolve import resolve
from gitversioned.targets import discover, stamp

__all__ = [
    "build_editable",
    "build_sdist",
    "build_wheel",
    "get_requires_for_build_editable",
    "get_requires_for_build_sdist",
    "get_requires_for_build_wheel",
    "prepare_metadata_for_build_wheel",
    "stamped",
]


@contextlib.contextmanager
def stamped(root: Path | None = None) -> Generator[str]:
    """
    Stamp every target for the length of a build, then restore tracked files.

    :param root: Project folder; defaults to the current one.
    :return: The resolved version in PEP 440 form.
    """
    config = load_config(root or Path.cwd())
    resolved = resolve(config)
    saved: dict[Path, str] = {}
    for target in discover(config):
        if not target.generated and target.path.is_file():
            saved[target.path] = target.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    stamp(config, resolved)
    try:
        yield resolved.version.pep440()
    finally:
        for path, text in saved.items():
            with path.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
                handle.write(text)


def _maturin() -> Any:
    """Import maturin lazily so the module loads without it."""
    import maturin  # noqa: PLC0415

    return maturin
```
